repositories.name: qala-lang
repositories.description: A statically typed teaching language where saying is doing. Effect annotations, scope-bound defer, an ARM64 backend, built in Rust with a WebAssembly playground.

paragraphs: A statically typed programming language where saying is doing.

Qala (قال) is the Arabic word for "he said" or "to say." In Arabic, when you say something with qala, you are making a declaration, stating what is. Qala the language works the same way. When you write a function marked is pure, it is pure. The compiler guarantees it. When you write defer close(f), the file closes. The compiler guarantees that too. There is no gap between what you write and what happens.

This is the core idea: a language where your code is a truthful declaration of behavior. Side effects are visible in function signatures. Resources are managed explicitly. Types are known before the program runs. Nothing is hidden, nothing is implicit, nothing surprises you.

whatItDoes.text: A statically typed programming language where saying is doing.

paragraphs: Додатково Chrome-розширення з extension/upwork-tracker пасивно читає вже завантажений DOM Upwork Messages і передає нові повідомлення backend. Backend прибирає дублікати, зіставляє room з активною задачею-проєктом у ClickUp і додає повідомлення коментарем. Нові ClickUp-задачі в цьому потоці не створюються.

Кидаєш боту завдання в будь-якій формі — текстом, скріншотом, PDF, DOCX, TXT/Markdown/CSV або поєднанням файла з коротким підписом. Бот прибирає з матеріалу службову переписку та згадки про команду або замовника, залишаючи лише те, що потрібно для виконання задачі. Сам текст задачі не перекладається і не переписується. Окремо уточнює, звідки взяти назву (назва файла, ID/заголовок у матеріалі або власна назва користувача) та дедлайн. Коли інформації достатньо — показує актуальний список виконавців із ClickUp, створює таску й надсилає посилання. Посилання зберігаються без змін і залишаються…
Якщо в задачі є посилання, бот не відкриває і не завантажує їх, а пропонує залишити, видалити або позначити як доступні лише в режимі інкогніто. Таску можна створити без виконавця.

repositories.name: Luau-decompiler
repositories.description: Explore this public GitHub project.

paragraphs: A static TypeScript decompiler for official Luau bytecode that aims for readable, source-like Luau instead of a register dump.
It never executes the input. The pipeline decodes the bytecode, reconstructs control flow and values, lifts them into an AST, and prints Luau:

A useful decompiler should recover program structure, not just rename registers. This project focuses on turning low-level bytecode patterns back into code that looks intentionally written while staying conservative when the original source cannot be proven.
features: structured if / elseif, value-if, loops, break, and continue
methods and closures instead of flat anonymous register operations
useful local and callback names when there is enough evidence
Roblox callback parameter names and types for common signals
tables, compound assignments, value packs, captures, and mutual recursion

whatItDoes.text: A static TypeScript decompiler for official Luau bytecode that aims for readable, source-like Luau instead of a register dump.

repositories.name: drydock
repositories.description: Open source container update monitoring — 23 registries, 21 triggers, audit log, OIDC auth, Prometheus metrics, and a modern dashboard.

paragraphs: English · Español · Polski · 简体中文 · Deutsch · Français · Português (Brasil)

Container images drift out of date silently. A base image patches a CVE, an app cuts a release, a tag moves. Unless you're watching every registry by hand, your running containers fall behind until something breaks or gets exploited.

Most tools force a tradeoff. The auto-updaters (Watchtower, Ouroboros) pull and restart with little visibility or control, and are now largely unmaintained. The dashboards (Portainer) manage containers but aren't built for update intelligence. Drydock is monitor-first: it watches 23 registries and tells you exactly what changed (major, minor, patch, or digest) before anything happens, then acts only when you let it. And it goes further than any of them. Trivy/Grype vulnerability scanning blocks unsafe updates, cosign verifies signatures, pre-update image backups roll back automatically on…

✅ = supported ❌ = not supported ⚠️ = partial / limited ? = unconfirmed † = archived, no longer maintained

Also compared: Dozzle v11 adds digest update checks, bulk and scheduled auto-update, safe swap and cleanup, but it is a log viewer first and has no column here. Komodo's column covers digest-only polling and…

paragraphs: This project is designed as an educational tool to demonstrate the risks and implications of broken access control vulnerabilities, specifically focusing on the unethical use of cookies to gain unauthorized access to web pages. It serves as a practical example for cybersecurity students, ethical hackers, and security professionals to understand how access control misconfigurations can be exploited and, more importantly, how to mitigate such vulnerabilities in real-world applications.

Broken Access Control occurs when a web application does not properly restrict access to its resources from users who are not supposed to access them. This can lead to unauthorized disclosure of information, modification of data, or execution of privileged operations. In this project, we focus on how attackers can exploit cookies to bypass access controls.

repositories.name: PulseFlow
repositories.description: Automated weather ETL pipeline: Open-Meteo to DuckDB to dbt to Streamlit

paragraphs: An automated weather ETL pipeline. Every 30 minutes it pulls current conditions and a 24-hour hourly forecast for 10 cities from the Open-Meteo API, validates and flattens the data, loads it into DuckDB, models it with dbt, and serves it through a Streamlit dashboard.
PulseFlow tracks live and forecast weather for 10 cities (Chennai, Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, London, New York, Tokyo, Singapore, Dubai, Sydney) using the free, key-less Open-Meteo API.

The live pipeline runs on a GitHub Actions schedule and commits the updated data/weather.duckdb back to the repo. An Airflow DAG mirrors the same extract → validate → transform → load logic as the production-equivalent orchestrator, for environments that need a "real" scheduler instead of CI cron.
features: Extract — fetch current weather + 24hr hourly forecast per city, save raw JSON.
Validate — check required fields exist and are non-null; skip and log bad records.
Transform — flatten current + hourly readings into tabular rows per city per timestamp.
Load — upsert rows into a weatherraw table in DuckDB.
Model — dbt cleans and types the raw data (staging) and computes daily per-city aggregates plus a temperature-anomaly flag (marts).

whatItDoes.text: An automated weather ETL pipeline. Every 30 minutes it pulls current conditions and a 24-hour hourly forecast for 10 cities from the Open-Meteo API, validates and flattens the data, loads it into DuckDB, models it with dbt, and serves it through a Streamlit dashboard.

repositories.name: ApexStore
repositories.description: Rust LSM-Tree storage engine with DashMap MemTable, SSTable auto-repair, and TLS support. Designed for embedding in applications that outgrow SQLite.

paragraphs: High-performance, embedded Key-Value engine built with Rust 🦀
Implementing LSM-Tree architecture with a focus on SOLID principles, observability, and performance.

ApexStore is a modern, Rust-based storage engine designed for write-heavy workloads. It combines the durability of write-ahead logging (WAL) with the efficiency of Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM-Tree) architecture.
features: Educational Clarity: A clean, modular implementation of LSM-Tree that serves as a blueprint for high-performance systems.
Strict SOLID Compliance: Leveraging Rust's ownership model to enforce clear boundaries between MemTable, WAL, and SSTable layers.
Observability First: Built-in real-time metrics for memory, disk usage, and WAL health.
Modern Defaults: Native LZ4 compression, Bloom Filters, encryption-at-rest (AES-GCM), and 45+ tunable parameters via environment variables.
Security Hardened: TLS/HTTPS support, CORS enforcement, rate limiting, per-IP connection limits, audit logging, and CSRF protection.

whatItDoes.text: High-performance, embedded Key-Value engine built with Rust 🦀

repositories.name: symphony-coord
repositories.description: Explore this public GitHub project.

paragraphs: Task & Plan-K → Capability-Guided Screening (CGS) → Contextual Bandit Routing (CBR) & CoT-P → Aggregate & Learn

Symphony-Coord is a task-local routing framework for multi-agent LLM systems. It formulates subtask-level executor selection as an online contextual bandit problem, using task information and observable service state.
Instead of relying on static expert assignment or handcrafted orchestration policies, Symphony continuously learns routing decisions from interaction outcomes.
features: Task & Plan-K: form candidate plans and ordered subtask chains.
Capability-Guided Screening (CGS): retain a Top-L shortlist using capability match, prior success, and reliability.
Contextual Bandit Routing (CBR) & CoT-P: select executors with LinUCB and collect repeated subtask outputs.
Aggregate & Learn: combine outputs by subtask-level majority voting and weighted cross-plan voting, then update the selector when action-linked feedback is resolved.
capability-guided, non-executing Top-L screening

repositories.name: UI-LAB
repositories.description: Live, runnable reference library of UI patterns for future frontends.

paragraphs: A design skill for coding agents, and the library behind it.

The skill makes an AI coding agent follow a short, gated procedure before it writes UI: write the brief, name the house style it would fall into by default and leave it, pick a direction from design worlds that differ, build, then render the page at 1440 px and a true 375 px and fix what the checks find before calling it done. It works in Claude Code and any agent that reads a SKILL.md skills folder.

The library is 263 working patterns (22 of them whole sites), each with a live demo, its code, when to use it and an accessibility note. Everything in it runs live, shows its code, and says how it behaves for people who use a keyboard or a screen reader.

whatItDoes.text: A design skill for coding agents, and the library behind it.

repositories.name: amp-atlas
repositories.description: Browser-only antimicrobial peptide research workspace: published data, molecular visualization, descriptors, and sequence/structure neighbors.

paragraphs: A browser-only antimicrobial peptide research workspace: published peptide records, interactive molecular visualization, transparent calculations, and sequence/descriptor/3D neighbor searches.

No rented server, API key, sign-in, remote inference or Python runtime is needed for visitors. The static website and its downloadable database are included in this repository. GitHub Pages serves public files; a Web Worker performs calculations on the visitor's device. Uploaded sequences and PDB files are never submitted to a server. GitHub may record ordinary page/data-file requests. External research links open the cited providers.
features: 12,784 DRAMP source records; 11,718 distinct sequence strings; 10,579 canonical records eligible for sequence calculations; 5,183 source SMILES annotations.
433 sequence-matched PDB chain structures, including multiple structures/chains for the same sequence; 315 DRAMP records have a local sequence-matched structure.
3Dmol.js all-atom molecular viewer: cartoon, sticks, spheres, lines, solvent-accessible surfaces, atom/residue identification, labels, rotation and PNG/PDB export.
Interactive inverse helical-wheel designer: choose 1–72 residues, fill numbered positions, read the linear N→C sequence, search partial positional constraints, and export FASTA/SVG.
Mass, charge versus pH, estimated pI, GRAVY, hydrophobic fraction, ideal-helix hydrophobic moment, aromaticity, reduced-cysteine extinction coefficient, amino-acid composition and plots.

whatItDoes.text: A browser-only antimicrobial peptide research workspace: published peptide records, interactive molecular visualization, transparent calculations, and sequence/descriptor/3D neighbor searches.

repositories.name: blok
repositories.description: AI-powered block-based rich text editor for the web, like the one in Notion

paragraphs: A block-based rich text editor for the web, like the one in Notion. Every paragraph, heading, image or list is its own block. You can drag it, nest it, or convert it into something else.

A plain contenteditable field hands you one HTML blob and leaves you to parse it. Blok saves typed JSON blocks instead. The same content can then go into a database column, be diffed between revisions, or be rendered on a server that never touches the DOM.
Blok is also headless. It ships the engine and the tools, not a theme, so the chrome is yours.
features: JSON in, JSON out. save() returns { id, type, data } blocks — no HTML parsing on your side.
Renders without a browser. @bloklabs/core/view turns saved documents into sanitized HTML synchronously, in Node, workers, or React Server Components.
React, Vue and Angular adapters. Separate packages that peer on the core, so the engine is never bundled twice. In React, is a real controlled component.
69 languages, RTL included. Locales lazy-load by browser language; right-to-left scripts lay out correctly.
CRDT-backed undo. History runs on Yjs: undo restores the caret, groups small edits, and batches atomically via blocks.transact().

whatItDoes.text: A block-based rich text editor for the web, like the one in Notion. Every paragraph, heading, image or list is its own block. You can drag it, nest it, or convert it into something else.

repositories.name: ask-your-data
repositories.description: Governed text-to-SQL over 71 synthetic tables: deterministic or model-assisted SQL, read-only structural controls, question-binding trace, returned-row verification, and voice/text answers.

paragraphs: This repo started as a Raspberry Pi voice assistant, became an analytics capstone, and now speaks again — with governed SQL between the question and the answer.

▶ Live demo: ask-your-data-kp.streamlit.app — type your own question. No API key required, and none is configured on the deployment: without one, the SQL is written by a deterministic compiler (engine/planner.py) that binds your words to the warehouse's own columns, values and join graph. Bring your own key in the sidebar to let a language model write SQL. Voice needs no key either — faster-whisper and Piper run inside the same process, so you can ask out loud and hear the answer back on the deployed app with nothing configured. Same guard, same verifier, same executor whether the question…

The interface is organized around four jobs: Ask keeps the governed answer flow focused, Data catalog searches authorized tables/columns/values, and Trust center collects identity scope, runtime controls, session telemetry, and a versioned release-assurance pack with benchmark, red-team, role-policy, and cost-envelope evidence. Project brief provides a two-minute recruiter walkthrough with inspectable engineering evidence and explicit limits. Model and voice settings stay collapsed until they are needed.

repositories.name: BIDSHIELD
repositories.description: BIDSHIELD is a sealed-bid Vickrey auction market settled entirely in shielded ZEC. Bids, escrow, refunds, and proceeds never touch a transparent address.

paragraphs: Sealed-bid Vickrey auctions, settled entirely in shielded ZEC.

Buyers place encrypted escrow bids straight from their wallet via ZIP-321 payment requests; the auctioneer never holds funds and never learns amounts on-chain. At close, a single batched shielded transaction pays the winner (second-price or buy-it-now), refunds every loser, pays the seller, and returns any seller collateral — all in one zsendmany, all Orchard notes, no transparent leg.
Competition submission for Zecathon 2026 — Private Markets.

whatItDoes.text: Sealed-bid Vickrey auctions, settled entirely in shielded ZEC.

requirements.text: Brings up the regtest stack (assumes docker compose up -d has been run once for the wallets), then runs the full product lifecycle — sign in, create lot, three sealed ZIP-321 bids, detect, close, Vickrey settle, verify shielded-only settlement — plus the security regression suite (authz boundaries, concurrent settle race, sealed dashboard, rate limiting).

Sign-in is by seed phrase: the server issues a nonce challenge, the browser derives a secp256k1 key from the 12/24-word seed (on a path unlinkable to the funds address) and signs the Zcash Signed Message payload, and the API issues an httpOnly session cookie.

repositories.name: outbound-lead-engine
repositories.description: Outbound lead generation pipeline: enrichment cascade over mock providers, measured cost per lead. Demo data only.

paragraphs: An outbound lead generation pipeline: company intake, an enrichment cascade that calls the cheapest data provider first, lead scoring, a "why this person, why now" hypothesis per segment, AI-written emails with validation, signed event ingest, and a kill switch that turns off hypotheses that don't get replies.

Demo mode by design. Every company and person is fictional, every domain ends in .example (reserved by RFC 2606, so no address can reach a mailbox), data providers are mocks with the real APIs' response shapes, and sending is a simulator. No real email is sent and no real person's data is processed. The LinkedIn Sales Navigator module from the original design stays documentation only: automating it breaks LinkedIn's terms and gets accounts banned.

Live: outbound-lead-engine.vercel.app (dashboard), fed by a GitHub Actions run started on demand, one simulated day per run: new emails written by an LLM, the simulator's events delivered over HTTPS to the signed webhook, the kill switch applied. All six stages are done; see Roadmap.

whatItDoes.text: An outbound lead generation pipeline: company intake, an enrichment cascade that calls the cheapest data provider first, lead scoring, a "why this person, why now" hypothesis per segment, AI-written emails with validation, signed event ingest, and a kill switch that turns off hypotheses that don't get replies.

paragraphs: Every sale split, booked, and invoiced. Your agency's numbers, handled.

repositories.description: Private market infrastructure with shielded Zcash settlement.

paragraphs: Veylora Market is an experimental privacy-focused Web3 deal desk for requests for quotation (RFQs) and competing offers. The first supported deal categories are OTC and token deals, DAO procurement, and Web3 services. A buyer publishes a request, suppliers submit offers, the buyer closes and awards the request under the current rule, and Zcash testnet settlement evidence is checked separately.

Status: testnet beta. Wallet connection and signature-based sign-in, persistent RFQ/offer storage, server-side award handling, category-aware Web3 requests, verified-testnet-wallet write policies, and a transparent-output testnet settlement verifier are implemented. The marketplace applies access controls to bid data, but has not been independently audited. Do not use it for valuable trades.

repositories.name: LGUI
repositories.description: Game UI framework for AI agents, made by LumioGames. Build screens, logic and tests in the browser with no game engine, then export to Unity. 给 AI Agent 用的游戏 UI 框架，不依赖游戏引擎。

paragraphs: LGUI is a game UI framework for AI agents, made by LumioGames. The source is public.

Building game UI usually starts with installing an engine, creating a project, and assembling screens in its editor. LGUI moves that work into the browser. Screens live in a ui/ folder in FairyGUI format, game code is TypeScript written in MVC style, previews open in the browser, and tests run in Node. Building screens, writing logic and checking screenshots all happen without opening a game engine, so an agent can do the work and check it too.

When you ship, lgui unity export exports the same screens and code to Unity, and the game code stays as it is. Game code only calls the lgui API and never touches the engine. A backend adapter handles the engine differences, and other engines can be added the same way.

whatItDoes.text: LGUI is a game UI framework for AI agents, made by LumioGames. The source is public.

repositories.name: cache-pulse
repositories.description: Check static hosting caching for performance: long max-age + immutable on fingerprinted assets, revalidation on HTML, no long cache on unhashed files, Vary and Set-Cookie pitfalls, and precompressed .br/.gz files that match. Reads _headers, vercel.json, netlify.toml, firebase.json. SARIF, Action. Zero deps.

paragraphs: Check that your static hosting config caches the right things: fingerprinted assets for a year, HTML revalidated, and nothing stale after a deploy.

Caching is the cheapest performance win and the easiest to get backwards. Fingerprinted bundles (index-BdT9x2Qa.js) should be cached for a year with immutable; HTML and unfingerprinted files (/styles.css, /logo.png) must revalidate, or visitors keep yesterday's site. cache-pulse reads the header rules in your build output or repo (headers, vercel.json, netlify.toml, firebase.json, serve.json), resolves the Cache-Control that applies to every file, and reports the mistakes, grouped by the header rule that causes them.

CLI, library and GitHub Action. Node.js 18+, zero runtime dependencies. Works on any static build output (Astro, Next.js output: 'export', Eleventy, Hugo, Jekyll, Docusaurus, VitePress, plain HTML) and runs offline: point it at the folder your build writes. By Louis Wright.
features: Fingerprinted assets: content-hashed file names and framework output folders (next/static, astro, app/immutable, nuxt, CRA static/js) need max-age=31536000, immutable; short, missing, no-cache and no-store policies are…
HTML: cached without revalidation or immutable is high severity; s-maxage for the CDN with max-age=0 for browsers is accepted.
Unfingerprinted files: immutable or a max-age over a week on /styles.css or /app.js means users do not see deploys; missing policies are noted.
Pitfalls: Vary: , Set-Cookie on static files (no CDN caching), Content-Encoding on images and fonts.
Compression: when the build ships .br/.gz files, every text asset over 1.4 kB should have one, and each is decompressed and compared with the original to catch stale copies.

whatItDoes.text: Check that your static hosting config caches the right things: fingerprinted assets for a year, HTML revalidated, and nothing stale after a deploy.

Contact form without a third party. Cloudflare Email Sending plus a D1 database that stores every submission before any email is attempted.
Backups. Daily encrypted Sanity exports to a GitHub artifact and to Cloudflare R2.

repositories.name: stellar-private-payments
repositories.description: Nethermind Privacy Engineering team's implementation of private payments for the Stellar network

paragraphs: This project is a Work in progress (WIP). It is intended to serve as a reference implementation of privacy pools for Stellar. The code has not yet been audited and should not be used in production environments with real assets as of now. The security hardening work is planned. Expect breaking changes and necessity to clear your local storage for the demo app/cli until the first stable release.

A privacy-preserving payment system for the Stellar network using zero-knowledge proofs. This implementation enables users to deposit, transfer, and withdraw tokens while maintaining transaction privacy through Groth16 proofs.

The system incorporates Association Set Provider (ASPs) as a control mechanism to provide illicit activity safeguards through association sets. ASPs maintain membership and non-membership Merkle trees that allow proving whether specific deposits are part of approved or blocked sets, enabling pool operators to enforce administrative controls without compromising user privacy.
features: Private Payments: Deposit, transfer, and withdraw tokens without revealing transaction amounts or sender/receiver relationships
Zero-Knowledge Proofs: Groth16 (over BN254) proofs generated via Circom circuits.
Administrative Controls: ASP-based membership and non-membership proofs for illicit activity safeguards
Browser-Based Proving: Client-side proof generation using WebAssembly
Stellar Integration: Built on Soroban smart contracts

Standard RAG — embed, retrieve top-k, stuff into prompt — fails quietly in two ways:
This project addresses both: a graph layer for relational/multi-hop questions, a router to pick between strategies, and instrumentation on every decision.
features: Multi-hop questions break it. "What company did the person who founded X later work for?" needs two facts that live in different chunks. The second fact may have near-zero semantic similarity to the original query, so…

features: 🔮 Proactive Memory. Proactivity is a property of the memory substrate, not the agent's policy — goals emerge from the topology that accumulates the conditions for them.

🧠 Architecture. A tri-layered substrate extending Complementary Learning Systems with a prefrontal Intent layer — events fold into concepts, concepts crystallize into intents, surfaced through a hierarchical context…

🌱 Conceptual Bootstrapping. Accumulation, compression, decay, completion — four structural debts of a streaming event log, resolved as transparent graph rewrites: test-time learning without gradient updates or surface…
📊 Evaluation. CogEval-Bench isolates proactive emergence from retrieval accuracy; seven downstream benchmarks confirm the substrate stays robust on conventional memory tasks.

repositories.name: Kollect
repositories.description: Your cluster, in Git, diffable — Kubernetes inventory operator: CRD-native GVK selection, CEL extraction, export to Git, databases, and streams.

paragraphs: Turn Kubernetes state into durable inventory. Declare what matters once. Kollect keeps it current and delivers it to Git, object storage, databases, and event streams. Select resources by GVK, extract the attributes you need with CEL or JSONPath, and every sink receives the same canonical rows in parallel.

Start with one sink. Grow to a whole platform. A single pipeline can write an inspectable Git history, a queryable database record, an object-store snapshot, or an event stream—without scripts or API-server hammering. As adoption grows, nothing gets rebuilt: the same rows fan out to more sinks, and KollectScope keeps it multi-tenant. Every team owns its inventory as configuration, not code, in its own namespace; consumers read export data, never unbounded list/watch against the live cluster.
Pre-1.0. Kollect is a public alpha with a v1alpha1 API: minor releases may break the API, defaults and export layout, and only the latest minor is supported. See Stability and support.

Pluggable sinks, no privileged backend — the same snapshot fans out to Git, Postgres, object
Multi-tenant by design — KollectScope gates which teams, namespaces, and sinks each tenant

paragraphs: Knee Osteoarthritis (OA) Detection using Deep Learning is an AI-powered clinical decision support system designed to assist in the early detection and severity assessment of Knee Osteoarthritis from X-ray images. Osteoarthritis is one of the most prevalent degenerative joint disorders worldwide, leading to chronic pain, reduced mobility, and diminished quality of life. Early and accurate diagnosis is essential for timely intervention and improved patient outcomes.

This project leverages deep learning techniques to automatically analyze knee X-ray images and classify disease severity based on the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system (Grades 0–4). Beyond prediction, the application incorporates Grad-CAM explainability to visualize the regions influencing the model's decisions, thereby enhancing transparency and clinical trust.
The solution is delivered through an intuitive Streamlit-based web application, enabling users to upload X-ray images and instantly receive:

paragraphs: A config-driven router that picks the right AI video model for every request, fails over when a provider goes down, and never charges a user for a failure.

Generative video products don't run on one model. They run on a portfolio: a cheap self-hosted model for the free tier, a lip-sync model for dialogue scenes, a premium model for hero shots. Each one is sold by several vendors, and all of them have outages, rate limits and content filters.

This repo is a small, runnable version of the routing pattern I designed while building a generative video platform in production. No API keys needed: providers are simulated so you can see every behavior in a few seconds.

whatItDoes.text: A config-driven router that picks the right AI video model for every request, fails over when a provider goes down, and never charges a user for a failure.

requirements.text: They run on a portfolio: a cheap self-hosted model for the free tier, a lip-sync model for dialogue scenes, a premium model for hero shots.

A production version also needs: async job polling (video generation takes minutes), per-vendor circuit breakers, health-weighted ordering, idempotency keys so a retry never double-generates, and cost/latency/quality telemetry feeding back into the catalog.

Since set 1's fixes, 0 of 15 recalled items were cleared green across 27 pre-registered cases. Tavily was the difference on recalls no database listed yet: with it off, all 10 in the first set were cleared green; with it on, 8 were flagged. On the 105 cases it was tuned on, it now gets 105 of 105 right and tags all…

Tagout checks what a household owns against live U.S. recalls. List what you own, or photograph the label. An agent on NVIDIA Nemotron (served by Nebius Token Factory) searches NHTSA, CPSC and the FDA with tools, and Tavily searches the agencies' newsrooms and USDA for anything the databases don't have yet. Nemotron reads each notice's list of affected models and lots, every code is checked against the notice's own text, and plain rules hang the tag. Save the list as a watch and a daily sweep reads every new recall once and matches it against the list; the watch's Atom feed tells you when one…

paragraphs: An autonomous deep research engine that transforms complex inquiries into interactive causal knowledge graphs, live agent dialogue, and chronological timelines.

When researching complex, multi-layered topics (geopolitical conflicts, industry disruptions, scientific breakthroughs, or historical inflection points), conventional AI search tools provide flat walls of text that are hard to verify, spatial relationships that are lost in linear prose, and opaque reasoning hidden behind loading spinners.

Tactile Ergonomics: Generous negative space, organic rounded image corners (rounded-2xl / rounded-xl), and bespoke SVG vector monogram artwork for an authentic print feel.
Strict Typographic Glyph Discipline: Zero emojis throughout editorial interfaces. Replaced by timeless typographic glyphs (✦, ◈, ◆, ❖, ⬡, —) and classical typography.

repositories.name: QACyberWatch
repositories.description: Phishing detection and brand protection for the State of Qatar: live Certificate Transparency monitoring, look-alike domain hunting and brand impersonation alerts for Qatari banks, payments, telecoms and government services.

paragraphs: Phishing detection and brand protection for the State of Qatar
Website · Live console · Qatar alignment · Protected brands · Changelog

Every certificate that browsers trust is written to public Certificate Transparency (CT) logs the moment it is issued. A phishing site that imitates a Qatari bank, the national payment switch, a ministry portal or a telecom operator therefore becomes visible in public data before the first message reaches a victim. QACyberWatch reads those logs directly, scores every hostname against Qatari brand profiles and local keywords, and turns look-alikes into triaged alerts that analysts can act on.
features: Early warning for the sectors NCSA, QCB and the ministries care about most: banking, payments, telecom, government e-services, health, energy, aviation and charity.
Evidence that organisations can use: STIX 2.1 bundles, CSV, reports, syslog and chat notifications feed existing SOC tooling and incident processes.
Full transparency: everything is open source, runs without a paid feed, and can be audited and extended by Qatari institutions, researchers and students.
Direct CT log tailing. Reads both RFC 6962 logs and Static CT API (tiled) logs with a built-in X.509 parser. No third-party aggregator, so nothing goes dark when a free feed does.
Correct shard selection. Reads every shard that newly issued certificates can land in, not only the shard whose window contains today.

whatItDoes.text: Phishing detection and brand protection for the State of Qatar

requirements.text: Knows the Qatari second-level suffixes (com.qa, net.qa, org.qa, gov.qa, edu.qa, mil.qa, name.qa, sch.qa), 80 other regional suffixes, 165 global suffixes and 77 free hosting platforms, so login.qnb.com.qa and qnb.com.qa.verify-login.example are never confused.

repositories.description: SparkDocs is an AI-powered document Q&A system that allows users to upload PDF, PPTX, or DOCX files, ask questions, and receive comprehensive answers based on the document's content.

paragraphs: Status: alpha. SparkDocs is a local-first document ingestion and grounded Q&A tool for PDF, DOCX, and PPTX files. It is intended for people who want to inspect ordinary documents with an explicit bring-your-own-key model rather than upload them to a managed document store.

SparkDocs validates and extracts documents in memory, builds structure-aware overlapping chunks, and retrieves evidence locally using dense embeddings plus BM25 keyword search. Reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) combines those results, a local cross-encoder reranks them, and only a bounded evidence set is sent in one Gemini request. Returned citation labels are restricted to retrieved locations; SparkDocs does not independently prove that every generated claim is entailed by its citation.

repositories.name: NLR-PSM3-2-EPW
repositories.description: Convert NREL PSM3 / NSRDB solar data into EnergyPlus Weather (EPW) files — Streamlit web app and Python tool for building energy simulation.

paragraphs: NLR-PSM3-2-EPW is a free, open-source Python tool and Streamlit web app that converts NREL Physical Solar Model (PSM v3.2.2 / v4.0.0, NSRDB) solar and meteorological data into EnergyPlus Weather (EPW) files for building energy simulation. Pick any location by latitude / longitude and download a ready-to-use .epw for a specific year or a Typical Meteorological Year (TMY).

Getting hourly weather data into an EnergyPlus-ready EPW file usually means manual API calls and column wrangling. This tool automates the full NSRDB → EPW pipeline — click a point on a map, choose a year or TMY, and download the weather file.

An EnergyPlus Weather (EPW) file is the standard hourly weather format consumed by EnergyPlus and most building energy simulation engines. It contains a full year (8760 hours) of solar, temperature, humidity, wind and sky-cover data for a single location, and is the starting point for energy modeling, daylighting and thermal-comfort analysis.
features: PSM3 / NSRDB → EPW conversion — turns NREL solar climate data into EnergyPlus Weather format.
Interactive map — pick a location by clicking, or enter latitude / longitude manually.
TMY and single-year datasets — download tmy, tgy, tdy, or a specific historical year (≥ 1998).
Resilient downloads — automatically falls back to core attributes when a dataset is
sparse at a location, so remote points still produce a valid EPW.

repositories.name: summarizer
repositories.description: A text and document summarizer made in python with the txtai library and hosted on Streamlit.

paragraphs: Abstractive summarization is the process of generating a summary of a text by understanding its meaning and creating a new text that conveys the same information in a shorter form. Abstractive methods employ more powerful natural language processing techniques to interpret text and generate new summary text, as opposed to selecting the most representative existing excerpts to perform the summarization. Read More

The app is built using "txtai" a powerful NLP library. Txtai builds embeddings databases, which are a union of vector indexes and relational databases. This enables similarity search with SQL. paragraphs: Welcome to the development hub for the WordPress Gutenberg project!

"Gutenberg" is a codename for a whole new paradigm in WordPress site building and publishing that aims to revolutionize the entire publishing experience as much as Gutenberg did the printed word. Right now, the project is in the second phase of a four-phase process that will touch every piece of WordPress -- Editing, Customization, Collaboration (which includes Real-time collaboration, Asynchronous collaboration, Publishing flows, Post revisions interface, Admin design, Library), and Multilingual -- and is focused on a new editing experience, the block editor.

The block editor introduces a modular approach to pages and posts: each piece of content in the editor, from a paragraph to an image gallery to a headline, is its own block. And just like physical blocks, WordPress blocks can be added, arranged, and rearranged, allowing WordPress users to create media-rich pages in a visually intuitive way -- and without workarounds like shortcodes or custom HTML.

repositories.name: yonedarepo-research
repositories.description: Source Code as a Transactional Abstraction: foundations for transactional source control (Delta Lake + Spark for code) with a serverless, Git-compatible realization. 4 papers + site.

paragraphs: Source code and source control are now transactional abstractions. This repository holds four papers that lay the foundations for that view, along with the website that presents them. In the model, a repository is a database, a change is a transaction with a read set and a write set, landing is an optimistic commit, a version is a snapshot, and derived data (search, symbols, checks, and Git itself) are views over the log.

The argument rests on precedent. Data lakes moved from files on object stores to tables with a transaction log, snapshots and optimistic concurrency (Delta Lake), with Spark-style computation over snapshots. Anthropic's published Scion design makes the same move for source control. The papers give definitions, proofs reduced to established results from data systems, and one working serverless realization with measured costs and open problems.

paragraphs: Zhuoyang Liu, Jiaming Liu, Hao Chen, Jiale Yu, Ziyu Guo, Chengkai Hou, Chenyang Gu, Xiangju Mi, Renrui Zhang, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Jian Tang, Pheng-Ann Heng, Shanghang Zhang

🤖LaST​0​ is a framework that enables efficient reasoning before acting through a Latent Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought (CoT), capturing fine-grained physical and robotic dynamics that are often difficult to verbalize. Specifically, we introduce a token-efficient latent CoT space that models future visual dynamics, 3D structural information, and robot proprioceptive states, and further extends these representations across time to enable temporally consistent implicit reasoning trajectories. Furthermore, LaST0 adopts a dual-system architecture implemented via a Mixture-of-Transformers…

repositories.name: acl
repositories.description: C/C++ server and network library, including coroutine,redis client,http/https/websocket,mqtt, mysql/postgresql/sqlite client with C/C++ for Linux, Android, iOS, MacOS, Windows, Harmony,etc..

paragraphs: Acl (Advanced C/C++ Library) is a powerful cross-platform network communication library and server programming framework that supports Linux, Windows, Solaris, FreeBSD, macOS, Android, iOS, and HarmonyOS. Numerous applications developed with Acl run on various devices, providing stable and reliable services to hundreds of millions of users.

The Acl project includes a rich set of functional modules: network communication, server framework, application protocols, various codecs, and more. It has built-in implementations of common network protocols such as HTTP/SMTP/ICMP/MQTT/Redis/Memcached/Beanstalk/Handler Socket, as well as complete codec libraries including XML/JSON/MIME/BASE64/UUCODE/QPCODE/RFC2047/RFC1035, etc. Additionally, Acl provides a unified abstract interface for mainstream databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite), enabling developers to write database applications more easily, quickly, and securely.

repositories.description: AG2 (formerly AutoGen): The Open-Source AgentOS.Join us at: https://discord.gg/sNGSwQME3x

paragraphs: AG2 is an open-source programming framework for building AI agents and facilitating cooperation among multiple agents to solve tasks. AG2 aims to streamline the development and research of agentic AI. It offers features such as agents capable of interacting with each other, facilitates the use of various large language models (LLMs) and tool use support, autonomous and human-in-the-loop workflows, and multi-agent conversation patterns.

The project is currently maintained by a dynamic group of volunteers from several organizations. Contact project administrators Chi Wang and Qingyun Wu via support@ag2.ai if you are interested in becoming a maintainer.
We have several agent concepts in AG2 to help you build your AI agents. We introduce the most common ones here.
features: Agents: Agent is the core building block — it talks to a model provider, calls tools, and returns a reply.
Tools: Plain Python functions, decorated with @tool, that the agent can invoke.
Human in the loop: Pause a run to collect confirmation or missing information from a person.
Orchestrating multiple agents: Coordinate several agents over a hub and typed channels using the Network.
The agent harness: Opt-in primitives layered onto an agent — persistent knowledge, context assembly, and history compaction.

repositories.name: agenda
repositories.description: Lightweight job scheduling for Node.js

paragraphs: A light-weight job scheduling library for Node.js
Jobs are run with priority in a first in first out order (so they will be run in the order they were scheduled AND with respect to highest priority).

For example, if we have two jobs named "send-email" queued (both with the same priority), and the first job is queued at 3:00 PM and second job is queued at 3:05 PM with the same priority value, then the first job will run first if we start to send "send-email" jobs at 3:10 PM. However if the first job has a priority of 5 and the second job has a priority of 10, then the second will run first (priority takes precedence) at 3:10 PM.
features: Complete rewrite in TypeScript (fully typed!)
Pluggable backend - MongoDB by default, implement your own (see Custom Backend Driver)
Real-time notifications - Use Redis, PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY, MongoDB Change Streams (Native) or custom pub/sub
MongoDB 6 driver support
touch() with optional progress parameter (0-100)

whatItDoes.text: A light-weight job scheduling library for Node.js

repositories.name: webdb
repositories.description: An ultra-lean, browser-native relational database engine.

paragraphs: An ultra-lean (<50 KB), and powerful browser-native relational database engine built from scratch in C compiled to WASM.
🚀 Launch Studio Playground • ⚡ Run Live Benchmarks • 📖 Documentation • 📐 Specifications

WebDB is an ultra-lightweight, relational database built from scratch specifically for the web. Think of it as SQLite reimagined for modern browsers—bringing true SQL capabilities, ACID transactions, and persistent storage to offline-first apps without multi-megabyte bundles or complex server headers.
features: 🪶 Tiny Footprint (<50 KB Wasm): Up to 90%+ smaller than ported desktop SQLite or Postgres (PGlite) builds.
⚡ True Relational Power: Fast filtering, indexing, aggregations, multi-column sorting, and joins—replacing cumbersome IndexedDB cursor queries.
🔄 Async VFS by Heart: Built from the ground up for asynchronous browser storage—clean non-blocking page faults with zero Emscripten Asyncify stack hacks or slow workarounds.
🌐 Embraces the Web Platform: Uses the browser instead of fighting it—delegating to native crypto.subtle, Intl, RegExp, Date, and Web Locks rather than packing redundant C libraries into Wasm.
💾 Reliable Offline Persistence: First-class storage with high-speed OPFS (desktop & workers) and IndexedDB (Safari, mobile WebViews, private browsing).

whatItDoes.text: An ultra-lean (<50 KB), and powerful browser-native relational database engine built from scratch in C compiled to WASM.

repositories.name: quits
repositories.description: Split costs with friends and settle up in the fewest payments. A React Native app for iOS, Android and the web (Expo, TypeScript).

paragraphs: Split costs with friends. Settle up in the fewest payments.
A React Native app for iOS, Android and the web.

Quits keeps a running score of who paid for what on a trip, in a flat or on a night out, then works out the fewest payments that make everyone square. One TypeScript codebase runs it on iOS, Android and the web. It works offline, and your groups stay on your device: there is no server.
features: Provably the fewest payments. A dynamic program over every subset of people finds the true minimum, not a greedy guess, and the app explains why the plan can't be shorter. How it works

Exact to the penny, in any currency. Money is held in integers and split by the largest remainder method, and currencies are converted in BigInt at the European Central Bank's rate for the day. How it works
Type it as you'd say it. "Ramen ¥4,800, Aiko paid, split with Ben and me" becomes an expense. A small scanner reads it: instant, offline and fully tested. How it works
Shared without a server. A whole group fits in a link, after the #, where no server ever sees it. How it works
An app on the web too. Install it from the browser and it opens offline. On a wide screen, the groups sit in a sidebar.

The layer uses masks that are generated in masking.py.

repositories.name: ABot-Recon
repositories.description: Streaming 3D reconstruction from only video input: Revisiting Local Context for Long-Horizon Streaming 3D Reconstruction

paragraphs: In one sentence: ABot-Recon reconstructs long video streams with a fixed 12-frame local context, composing current-frame geometry and adjacent relative poses into a global reconstruction without persistent learned long-range memory.

Long-horizon streaming reconstruction is often approached by adding increasingly elaborate mechanisms for retaining and fusing long-range state. ABot-Recon takes a deliberately local route. At each time step, it solves the same bounded prediction problem:

This design keeps model-state memory and per-frame computation independent of the elapsed sequence length. A lightweight motion-visual rotation refiner and composition-aware pose loss are used to limit drift when local poses are composed over long horizons.
features: cache KV features from the preceding 11 frames;
predict a point map $Pi$ in the current camera coordinate system;
estimate the adjacent relative pose $T{i-1\leftarrow i}$; and
recover the global trajectory and point cloud through sequential pose composition.

whatItDoes.text: In one sentence: ABot-Recon reconstructs long video streams with a fixed 12-frame local context, composing current-frame geometry and adjacent relative poses into a global reconstruction without persistent learned long-range memory.

repositories.description: Skydiving weather dashboard for the Lincoln Sport Parachute Club (Brown's Airport, NE69). Flags conditions against published USPA and FAA limits with the rule behind each. Always use your own judgment and follow USPA guidelines, drop zone policies and your S&TA's instructions.

paragraphs: A skydiving weather dashboard for the Lincoln Sport Parachute Club (Brown's Airport, NE69) in Weeping Water, NE — tuned to the conditions that matter for jumpers and the club's Cessna 182 jump plane.

It consolidates the manual three-site routine (NOAA hourly forecast + usairnet cloud forecast + KPMV METAR) into one page, and adds winds aloft for freefall drift and density altitude for jump-plane climb performance.

In development — not endorsed or approved by USPA, LSPC, or any licensed professional. Advisory only. This dashboard flags conditions and cites guidance — it does not decide whether it's safe to jump. Every USPA, CFR and FAA citation here began as an AI recollection. Each has since been read at its source — the USPA SIM at uspa.org on 2026-09-22 (2-1 I, 2-2 and 4-7 again on 2026-10-08), the CFR sections, AIM 7-1-7 and FAA-P-8740-2 on 2026-09-23 — and the claims corrected against them. The club's wind-limit tiers are different in kind: a transcription of an undated photo of the posted sign,…

whatItDoes.text: A skydiving weather dashboard for the Lincoln Sport Parachute Club (Brown's Airport, NE69) in Weeping Water, NE — tuned to the conditions that matter for jumpers and the club's Cessna 182 jump plane.

repositories.name: planisphere
repositories.description: Print a star wheel for any latitude and any century: precession-accurate planispheres, ready to print or laser-cut.

paragraphs: Print a star wheel and inspect the astronomy behind every point. Compare stellar epochs from 3000 BCE to 3000 CE, then cut out the instrument.

A planisphere is a rotating star chart: dial in a date and time and a window shows the stars above your horizon. Its disc depends on latitude and stellar epoch. This app generates both the disc and its physical holder, then lets you trace a star from its catalogue record through motion and precession to the printed point. The historical view is a model with explicit limits, including an independent Gregorian date scale; it is not a reconstruction of ancient observing conditions. It pairs with horologium (ancient calendars) and gnomon (sundials).

Southern chart correction: the earlier south-pole projection reflected constellation shapes and compass directions. The wheel, date/hour scales and drag direction now follow an outward-looking sky map in both hemispheres. Replace both pieces of a previously generated southern instrument. Independent projection, original downloads and correction.
features: Bright-star catalogue: 2,865 stars to magnitude 5.5, reduced from the
HYG v4.1 database (J2000 coordinates, proper motion, distance, radial velocity, and B-V colour index), with pinned source revision and checksum.
Precession + proper motion for any epoch from 3000 BCE to 3000 CE
(IAU 2006/P03 model), applied live as you move the epoch slider. Motion propagates a Cartesian space vector with perspective when distance and radial velocity are available.
Find and inspect a star by name, designation, constellation or HIP/HYG

repositories.name: multiple-identity-providers-amazon-api-gateway
repositories.description: This example demonstrates a pattern to leverage multiple identity providers with an API Gateway and manage Authorization with Amazon Verified Permissions.

paragraphs: In many cases, enterprises need to build a unified access control layer to their APIs that allow access from multiple sources (for example multiple identity providers or different user groups and categories). One common use case would be an API exposed to different tenants through API Gateway, which can be supported by an Amazon Cognito multi-tenancy solution. For example, two Amazon Cognito User-pools could be created for an application, one for patients and another for healthcare providers with a common API that is used to provide access.

In addition to Amazon Cognito, developers can use Amazon API Gateway to manage, and expose APIs to provide access to back end resources. API Gateway is a fully managed service that allows developers to build APIs that acts as an entry point for applications and allows access to data, or functionality running on EC2, ECS, Lambda or any web application. To integrate with multiple IDPs, an AWS Lambda authorizer is used to control access to the API with Amazon Cognito as an identity provider. The Lambda authorizer enables customization of API authorization, and in this case allows multiple IDPs…

Amazon Verified Permissionsis a standalone service used to implement fine-grained authorization on resources in an application. Amazon Cognito is used to provide the authentication function for users prior to being authorized by Amazon Verified Permissions. All four services are leveraged together to combine multi IDPs into a centralized application access solution. The solution isn't limited to the Amazon Cognito IDP, any third party identity provider that generates JWTs can be used.

repositories.name: AxiomLab
repositories.description: A digital logic simulator that runs entirely in your browser. Drag gates onto a canvas, wire them up and watch signals travel in real time, with flip-flops, a live truth table and simplified Boolean expressions. Apple-inspired design. No install, no account.

paragraphs: Most logic simulators feel like lab software. AxiomLab is built to feel like a native Apple app (calm, glassy and springy) while being a real simulator underneath.

Place AND, OR, XOR and friends on a large, free-panning canvas. Wire them with clean right-angled lines. Flip a switch and watch a pulse of light race down the wire, through the gates, and into the output. Run a clock and watch a flip-flop count. Then open the truth table and see AxiomLab work out the simplest Boolean expression for your circuit on its own.
It is made for students learning digital electronics, teachers who want something better than a whiteboard, and anyone who simply enjoys watching logic work.
features: | Real signals, not decoration Three-valued logic (0, 1 and undefined X) with topological evaluation, so a circuit behaves the way the textbook says it should. | Light that travels When a wire turns on, the glow runs…
A dot-grid workspace with smooth, spring-driven pan and zoom. Zoom stays anchored under your cursor, from 25% to 400%.
A minimap, and one-tap Origin and Fit circuit buttons that glide the view where you need it.
Rendering is snapped to whole device pixels, so lines and dots stay crisp on any screen.
Gates snap to the grid, can never overlap, and can never leave the workspace. Drop one on top of another and it finds the nearest free spot.

whatItDoes.text: Most logic simulators feel like lab software. AxiomLab is built to feel like a native Apple app (calm, glassy and springy) while being a real simulator underneath.

repositories.name: huginn-proxy
repositories.description: High-performance reverse proxy forwarding TLS (JA4), HTTP/2 (Akamai), and TCP-SYN (eBPF-powered) fingerprints as HTTP headers

paragraphs: ghcr.io/biandratti/ — huginn-proxy, huginn-proxy-plain, huginn-proxy-ebpf-agent (images & layout)
High-performance reverse proxy with passive fingerprinting capabilities powered by Huginn Net.

Huginn Proxy is a reverse proxy built on Tokio, Hyper, and Rustls. It routes incoming connections to backend services while passively extracting TLS (JA4), HTTP/2 (Akamai), and TCP SYN (p0f-style) fingerprints and injecting them as headers. TCP SYN fingerprinting is implemented via an XDP/TC eBPF program using Aya. Fingerprinting libraries are provided by Huginn Net.

routes, backends, pools, headers, security filters, rate limits, …) hot-reload on SIGHUP or file-watch; static sections (listen, TLS, fingerprint flags, logging, telemetry, timeouts, …) need a restart (reload ignores…
IPv4 & IPv6 Dual-Stack - Listen on both address families simultaneously with per-family eBPF maps
HTTP/1.x & HTTP/2 - Full support for both protocol versions
Load Balancing - Round-robin load balancing across multiple backends

repositories.name: toolsuite
repositories.description: A privacy-first all-in-one toolkit for file conversion, PDF tools, media processing, developer utilities, LaTeX, and more.

paragraphs: A free, privacy-first all-in-one utility site for files, media, documents, and developer tasks.
Core principle: nothing you upload is ever stored. Every tool below runs 100% in your browser — no server, no database, no account. Close the tab and your file is gone, the way it should be.

Every tool above except LaTeX has a real, mature browser-side implementation: pdf-lib + pdfjs-dist for PDFs, the Canvas API for images, tesseract.js (WASM) for OCR, jszip for archives, SheetJS for Excel, ffmpeg.wasm (a real WASM build of FFmpeg) for video/audio, Web Crypto (SubtleCrypto) for hashing. That means the "no permanent storage" promise isn't a policy you have to trust for those tools — there's no upload endpoint for a file to ever reach.

whatItDoes.text: A free, privacy-first all-in-one utility site for files, media, documents, and developer tasks.

requirements.text: Every tool below runs 100% in your browser — no server, no database, no account.

repositories.description: Haunted Inbox: one hidden line in a patient message makes a hospital AI assistant leak another patient's chart. Gemma 4 12B, fully local via Ollama, plus Warding Circle mode: closed by design for these two harms. Built at Hacktoberfest Hack Day Brooklyn 2026.

paragraphs: One hidden line in a patient message can make a hospital's AI assistant leak another patient's restricted health record. Haunted Inbox shows the attack, scores it, and shows a system design that closes these two harms.

Wisp is the internal AI assistant at Hollowveil Memorial Hospital. It drafts replies to patient portal messages so staff can answer faster. Wisp runs on Gemma 4 12B, fully local: no cloud model and no API key. Messages go only to the Ollama server you run.

One message in Wisp's inbox looks like an ordinary request to move an appointment. It also carries lines that a person never sees but the model reads: ghosts. Haunted Inbox shows what those ghosts make a typical assistant do, scores it on a possession meter, and shows a design, Warding Circle mode, that is closed by design for these two harms.

paragraphs: Correlating internet outages with natural disasters, armed conflict, and government shutdowns.

A real-data pipeline that detects internet connectivity outages worldwide and attributes each one to a likely cause — natural disaster, armed conflict, government-ordered shutdown, or unexplained/technical failure — using only free, open-access data sources. Internet connectivity signal loss is treated as a real-time proxy for physical infrastructure damage — often faster and more granular than official reporting.

whatItDoes.text: Correlating internet outages with natural disasters, armed conflict, and government shutdowns.

requirements.text: Configure API keys as repository secrets and it starts producing live data with zero local setup — IODA and GDACS need no key at all, so it's useful even with none configured.

The original project spec included it as a curated disaster-event archive, but it's bulk-download-only with a days-to-weeks lag — GDACS already covers real-time disaster attribution here with no key and no registration friction, so EM-DAT would have added the same cause: disaster category at a real latency cost for no coverage gain this project needed.

repositories.name: fun-20260529-a-buffer-relay
repositories.description: Two-slot packet relay browser puzzle

paragraphs: Buffer Relay is a tiny browser puzzle about routing a packet stream through only two memory slots. Store incoming packets, emit the right slot, and match the target output before the relay desyncs.
It turns an abstract systems idea into a quick tactile challenge. The game makes limited memory feel concrete: you only have two slots, and every overwrite can make the target sequence impossible.

The puzzles are small enough to learn in one round but still reward planning. Clean pair flips build combo points, wrong emits create glitches, and perfect runs feel like snapping a tiny packet machine into sync.
features: It is a complete no-build browser toy that can be inspected, forked, and hosted as-is.
The rules are compact but teach a real constraint: two live buffers are enough only when you plan the emit order.
Challenge links and local-best storage make it easy to compare clean runs without accounts, servers, or tracking.

whatItDoes.text: Buffer Relay is a tiny browser puzzle about routing a packet stream through only two memory slots. Store incoming packets, emit the right slot, and match the target output before the relay desyncs.

Real diagnostics from the compiler, not guesses
Rename and code-action edits returned for the client to apply
Call and type hierarchies, symbol search, formatting, inlay hints, selection and folding ranges

repositories.name: psst-secret
repositories.description: A secure secret sharing platform

paragraphs: A privacy-focused, zero-knowledge app for sharing secrets securely. We call them whispers. All encryption and decryption happens in the browser — the server never sees your plaintext. By default, encrypted data and public key material are stored only in volatile memory (Redis with persistence disabled) and never touch disk.

The fragment is the part of a URL after #. RFC 3986 §3.5 reserves it for browser-side processing, and RFC 9110 §7.1 excludes it from HTTP requests. Key material in the fragment is therefore not sent to the server or included in HTTP request logs. Password-protected view links contain no decryption key fragment.
features: Zero-knowledge architecture — whispers are encrypted client-side with AES-256-GCM using the Web Crypto API. Decryption key material stays in the view link's URL fragment or is protected by your password.

In-memory ciphertext storage — encrypted data and public key material are stored in Redis with persistence disabled (--save "" --appendonly no) by default. Ciphertexts never touch disk in this configuration. If Redis…
Send mode — encrypt a whisper (text or file) and get a shareable link.

Receive mode — create a request using X-Wing, a hybrid of ML-KEM-768 (post-quantum, FIPS 203) and X25519. Share a submit link containing the public-key fingerprint and keep a separate view link containing the private…
Post-quantum ready — send mode uses 256-bit symmetric encryption; receive mode uses hybrid key exchange, which remains protected as long as either component holds.

whatItDoes.text: A privacy-focused, zero-knowledge app for sharing secrets securely. We call them whispers. All encryption and decryption happens in the browser — the server never sees your plaintext. By default, encrypted data and public key material are stored only in volatile memory (Redis with persistence disabled) and never touch disk.

paragraphs: Note: The main branch may be in an unstable or even broken state during development. Please use releases instead of the main branch in order to get a stable set of binaries.

Harbor is an open source trusted cloud native registry project that stores, signs, and scans content. Harbor extends the open source Docker Distribution by adding the functionalities usually required by users such as security, identity and management. Having a registry closer to the build and run environment can improve the image transfer efficiency. Harbor supports replication of images between registries, and also offers advanced security features such as user management, access control and activity auditing.

Harbor is hosted by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF). If you are an organization that wants to help shape the evolution of cloud native technologies, consider joining the CNCF. For details about who is involved and how Harbor plays a role, read the CNCF announcement.
features: Cloud native registry: With support for both container images and Helm charts, Harbor serves as registry for cloud native environments like container runtimes and orchestration platforms.
Role based access control: Users access different repositories through 'projects' and a user can have different permission for images or Helm charts under a project.

Policy based replication: Images and charts can be replicated (synchronized) between multiple registry instances based on policies with using filters (repository, tag and label). Harbor automatically retries a…
Vulnerability Scanning: Harbor scans images regularly for vulnerabilities and has policy checks to prevent vulnerable images from being deployed.

LDAP/AD support: Harbor integrates with existing enterprise LDAP/AD for user authentication and management, and supports importing LDAP groups into Harbor that can then be given permissions to specific projects.

repositories.name: tastemaker
repositories.description: A Claude Code skill that grounds AI-generated UI in real reference images and a persistent per-developer taste profile, instead of generic AI-slop defaults.

paragraphs: A skill that gives AI real design taste, so the UI it builds does not look AI-generated.

Ask any model to build a UI and you tend to get the same thing: an indigo to purple gradient, a soft shadow card, a generic hero. This is not a prompting problem. It happens because the model has to invent taste from a text description, with nothing real to ground it and no memory of what you actually like.
Tastemaker fixes this with four ideas, not a bigger catalog of canned options to pick from:
features: Generate within a check that actually runs. There is no fixed list of color combinations shipped with this skill, and the palette is not five approved colors the model may combine however it likes either. A new one is…

Ground in real pixels, not words. Give it a screenshot or a reference and it reads the real colors and contrast from the actual image, using a script. It does not write a vague summary of the vibe and rebuild from that.…

Remember, do not re-derive. Once a project locks a style, every later screen reuses it. Nothing drifts. Across projects, a small profile file learns what you keep and what you reject, so your next project starts warm.
Scope to the real work. It reads your spec first and figures out which screens actually need design, instead of dumping a design system that has nothing to do with what you are shipping.

whatItDoes.text: A skill that gives AI real design taste, so the UI it builds does not look AI-generated.

repositories.name: kandy-pm25-explorer
repositories.description: Interactive 1 km hourly PM2.5 explorer for Kandy, Sri Lanka (2019-2023): heatmap, terrain wind, uncertainty, decomposition, exposure and documented haze episodes. Static, client-reconstructed from a T-locked additive model.

paragraphs: A fully static web app showing fine-particle air pollution (PM2.5) over the Kandy valley, Sri Lanka, at 1 km and hourly since 2019: the valley in 3-D with this hour's haze, the hour's answer on one card (valley average, 90 % range on a WHO-anchored scale, regional background vs what the valley adds), detail in a drawer (Air mass · Where · Weather · Data) and time along the bottom (this day hour by hour, every day since 2019). Design "A / The Valley", 2026-10-29; the previous design is kept as git tag v2-valley-breathes.

No backend. The production model is T-locked, PM = B + max(T−B,0)·P + min(T−B,0) + ε(P−1), so the browser rebuilds any hour exactly from a compact payload (month chunks loaded on demand; first visit ≈ 3 MB).

Where in the valley. The within-valley pattern is physics, not a measurement (Kandy has one regulatory station). The Where tab therefore builds the family of patterns the evidence cannot tell apart (confinement strength k = 0–0.45 × satellite surface or terrain only, every one with this hour's valley average) and colours only what they all agree on. Town-to-town answers give a size from monitored valley cities (about 13 % for places 3–10 km apart), never a direction.

whatItDoes.text: A fully static web app showing fine-particle air pollution (PM2.5) over the Kandy valley, Sri Lanka, at 1 km and hourly since 2019: the valley in 3-D with this hour's haze, the hour's answer on one card (valley average, 90 % range on a WHO-anchored scale, regional background vs what the valley adds), detail in a drawer (Air mass · Where · Weather · Data) and time along the bottom (this day hour by hour, every day since 2019). Design "A / The Valley", 2026-10-29; the previous design is kept as git tag v2-valley-breathes.

repositories.name: palette-provider
repositories.description: 🎨 Extract intelligent color palettes from images using hybrid median-cut + k-means clustering in OKLAB perceptual space. Auto-classified into dominant, supporting, and accent tiers. React · Vite · Canvas. Live demo.

paragraphs: Extract intelligent color palettes from any image

src="./public/palette-provider.png" width="100%" alt="Palette Provider title art: the wordmark beside a photograph overlaid with the samples feeding its largest color family, a palette panel in family order, and a hue-density ridge below with a peak for every family fanning into its shades."

Palette Provider finds the color families in an image as density peaks in the OKLAB perceptually uniform color space, so a small but distinct color (down to about 1% of the image) is not lost inside a large one. The app shows the palette next to the analysis behind it: how much of the image each family covers, where each family sits in color space, and which pixels fed it.
features: Color Families — Every perceptually distinct color in the image becomes a family with a faithful color and its true share, whether it covers 60% of the image or 2%.
Detail Levels — Essential (one shade per family), Balanced (up to two), or Rich (up to three). Detail adds depth within families; it never adds or removes families.

Color Limit — Show every color, or at most 8, 5, or 3 swatches. When the palette is over the limit, the closest families merge until their shades fit, so Detail decides how the swatches are spent: distinct colors…

Palette Strip — Every color in one strip, ordered by Prevalence (largest shades first) or Family (each family's shades together, families around the hue wheel). Tap a color to copy it and select its family.
Breakdown — Each family as a bar as long as its share of the image, split into its shades, with every shade's value and share.

whatItDoes.text: Extract intelligent color palettes from any image

paragraphs: µprint ("micro print", written uprint wherever µ isn't available, as in hostnames) turns an ESP32-S3 into a small print server for your 3D printer or pen plotter. You upload G-code in the browser, µprint stores it on a microSD card or in its internal flash and streams it to the machine over USB. Start, pause and cancel from the browser on your computer or phone. No PC needs to keep running. µprint works with 3D printers running Marlin or Prusa firmware over USB (for example the Prusa MK3S) and with AxiDraw / NextDraw pen plotters (EiBotBoard).
features: Web interface in English and German, for desktop and phone, no app needed
Storage on microSD and, depending on the board, internal flash (up to about 12 MB)
Print control: start, pause (nozzle lifted), resume, cancel (heaters off, lift, park), progress and time left
(taken from the slicer's M73 when the file has it)
Printer-side actions: filament runout, pause and stop on the printer's own display, and questions the printer

repositories.name: doppler
repositories.description: Explore this public GitHub project.

paragraphs: Practical, portable, performant digital signal processing.

doppler is a C99 DSP library — NCO, FIR, FFT, polyphase resampling, DDC, AGC, carrier and burst acquisition, DSSS receivers, convolutional and Reed-Solomon coding, CCSDS framing and more — with file, buffer, and NATS-based streaming, and a scenario-driven waveform generator (wfmgen) with byte-identical CLI/Python/C parity. Python and Rust wrap the same C core — no second implementation, no divergence, full SIMD throughput from any language.
New here? Start with Start Here — a one-page map from "what are you trying to do" to the right doc.

repositories.name: r2u
repositories.description: CRAN as Ubuntu Binaries

paragraphs: We generally support amd64 (i.e. standard 64-bit Intel/AMD cpus, sometimes also called x86\64) for the current Ubuntu LTS release and its predecessor release, and support arm64 on the current release (more on this here). We use 'r-release' just like CRAN. So generally support (at least) the two most current LTS releases: currently 'jammy' 22.04 LTS and 'noble' 24.04 releases are fully supported with 'resolute' 26.04 ready for its upcoming release. The 'focal' 20.04 LTS release was the first one supported, and remains avaialble but (as of July 2025) no longer receives new updates.

Support for additional cpu architectures is certainly possible but somewhat unlikely due to a lack of (additional hardware) resources and time. Support for other distributions is possible but unlikely right now (due to a lack of resources and time). P3M/PPM/RSPM now appears to also support Debian which could be added at some later point.

Current versions are built under R 4.6.0 and are usable under the current R 4.6.0. BioConductor release 3.23 packages are provided when required by CRAN packages for resolute, noble and jammy; focal is at 3.21. Binaries were initially R 4.4.x based and are now built under R 4.6.0. Some older packages released when we used R 4.2.x or 4.3.x may have been built with R 4.2.x or R 4.3.x, they will still work the same with R 4.4.x as R is generally forward-compatible. There are exceptions (due to how R Core changes this) so if you notice an older package not loading please file an issue.
features: Full integration with apt as every binary resolves all its dependencies: No more
installations (of pre-built archives) only to discover that a shared library is missing. No more surprises.
Full integration with apt so that an update of a system library cannot break an R package:
if a (shared) library is used by a CRAN, the package manager knows, and will not remove it. No more (R package) breakage from (system) library updates.
Simpler and lighter than some alternatives as only run-time library packages are installed as

repositories.name: corridor-in-a-box
repositories.description: Manifest-driven engine for Stellar SEP-31 cross-border corridors - a corridor is config, not code.

paragraphs: An open, manifest-driven engine for Stellar SEP-31 cross-border corridors. A corridor is configuration, not code: the engine runs quote → comply → settle → reconcile → recover over any standards-compliant anchor pair, and adding a new corridor is a new .corridor.yaml file — not a fork.

Live demo: corridor-in-a-box.vercel.app — the corridor dashboard and a payment walkthrough. The walkthrough is a simulation: it drives a re-implementation of the state machine and never touches the Stellar network. ng-cowrie is the one exception in the demo's bundled lanes: its endpoints were probed against Cowrie's production API on 2026-08-11 — SEP-10 signed a challenge, SEP-12 answered, and SEP-31 /info returned a non-empty receive list — so it renders VERIFIED. That means endpoints were checked, not that money moved: Cowrie publishes no SEP-38 quote server, no payment has been attempted,…

This repo contains the open, runnable corridor engine and the RouteResolver seam. The intended open-core design leaves room for a proprietary anchor health/conformance dataset and route intelligence to be supplied through that interface, but neither that component nor a separate private repo is included here. The current default resolver lets the open repo run corridors on its own. Everything in this repo is publishable as-is.

whatItDoes.text: An open, manifest-driven engine for Stellar SEP-31 cross-border corridors. A corridor is configuration, not code: the engine runs quote → comply → settle → reconcile → recover over any standards-compliant anchor pair, and adding a new corridor is a new .corridor.yaml file — not a fork.

requirements.text: scripts/reference-anchor.sh up stands up the SDF Anchor Platform reference server locally under podman — a conformant SEP-31 counterparty, no agreements and no credentials required. pnpm fund:testnet then gives the sending account a USDC trustline and balance, and pnpm testnet drives a payment across it.
The signer must be a testnet account holding the corridor's bridge asset (USDC from the issuer the anchor quotes) with a trustline for it.

repositories.name: TokenTour
repositories.description: 「Token 之旅」交互式 LLM/Agent 教程

paragraphs: A vertical cross-section of the LLM application stack—from Agent messages to tokens and KV cache.

LLM applications look simple from the outside, but a single turn passes through many layers: Agent messages, chat templates, tokenization, the context window, attention, and KV cache. Each layer has its own representation, and the connections between them are easy to lose.

TokenTour makes a vertical cut through that stack. Instead of explaining one layer in isolation, it follows the same conversation downward and shows how a change at one level propagates through the rest.
features: Messages → chat template: compare how model families such as Qwen3, DeepSeek-V3, and GPT-OSS serialize the same conversation and tool calls.
Text → tokens: inspect token boundaries, byte-level behavior, and how small edits change the sequence.
Tokens → context and KV cache: see causal attention, estimate KV memory, and visualize which prefix could be reused on the next turn.
Cross-layer tracing: hover or select an item to follow the corresponding region across the synchronized views.

whatItDoes.text: A vertical cross-section of the LLM application stack—from Agent messages to tokens and KV cache.

requirements.text: The playground includes prepared Agent traces, so no API key is needed.
