repositories.name: liquid-composer
repositories.description: The Web Icon Composer. Design OS 27 Liquid Glass right in your browser.

paragraphs: Design Liquid Glass app icons in the browser.

Liquid Composer is a web recreation of Apple's Icon Composer that reproduces the Liquid Glass icon material of iOS 27 and Icon Composer 2. Drop in your artwork, stack it in layers, and the engine renders the glass in real time: light from above, highlights and dark edges that define each shape, refraction between layers, background blur, translucency and layer shadows, composited inside the iOS squircle.

Rendering runs on a WebGL2 pipeline. A distance field of each layer's silhouette drives refraction and edge lighting; when Blur is on, two separable Gaussian passes blur everything beneath the layer, and the glass composite shader works in gamma-encoded sRGB, like Icon Composer. Without WebGL2 the app falls back to Canvas 2D: layers keep their shadow, translucency and edge lighting, but lose refraction and blur.
features: Layer-based editing with one level of groups, drag-and-drop reordering, inline rename, duplicate and undo/redo
SVG, PNG and JPEG import. SVGs are re-rasterized at render resolution so edges stay crisp
Glass controls per layer, or applied to all layers at once: Specular placement, Refraction (Strength, Height), Blur, Translucency and Shadow
Advanced panel with Lens (Dispersion), Highlights (Light intensity, Top, Bottom, Edge definition) and Surface (Frostiness), with a reset
Per-layer opacity, blend mode, and solid or two-stop gradient fill

repositories.name: Matryoshka
repositories.description: MCP server for token-efficient large document analysis via the use of REPL state

paragraphs: Process documents 100x larger than your LLM's context window—without vector databases or chunking heuristics.
features: The resource-limit features remain runRLM-only. The recursive primitives (rlmquery/rlmbatch) work in both paths — the MCP path spawns a child runRLMFromContent whose llmClient is the same sampling bridge as the parent,…
runRLM: children fan out concurrently via a worker pool capped at maxConcurrentSubcalls (default 4).

lattice-mcp: children run sequentially because the multi-turn suspension protocol can carry only one pending request at a time. Round-trip count is identical to the concurrent path (N children × M turns each); only…
Per-doc line numbers come back, so the LLM can cite "doc 0 line 4, doc 2 line 2" with confidence rather than inventing absolute offsets across a concatenation.
The partial answer is always preserved when present — completed work is never silently lost on abort.

repositories.name: legal-auditor-ai
repositories.description: Contract clause classifier: fine-tuned LegalBERT on CUAD, 88.4% accuracy on unseen contracts. Streamlit app with risk flags, explanations and PDF reports.

paragraphs: Legal Auditor AI takes a contract (pasted text or a PDF), splits it into clauses and classifies each clause with a fine-tuned LegalBERT model into one of 19 clause types (Governing Law, Limitation of Liability, Anti-Assignment, Audit Rights, ...) or Other. Each clause gets a risk level and the words that influenced the prediction most.

It then asks the opposite question: which clause types should be in this contract and are not? A distribution agreement with no Limitation of Liability and no Audit Rights is unusual, and that is a finding no per-clause label can express. "Unusual" is measured, not assumed — against the base rates of the 510 annotated contracts, within the same contract type where there is enough data for one.
The labels come from CUAD, a public dataset of 510 commercial contracts annotated by lawyers.

repositories.name: goodfellow-cms
repositories.description: Goodfellow CMS is a git-based website builder on the Puck visual editor. Non-technical owners edit pages at /admin, and every change is saved as a commit in the site’s own GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repository. No server or database.

paragraphs: A git-based website builder built on the Puck visual editor.

Goodfellow gives non-technical site owners a drag-and-drop editor at /admin with no server, database or monthly hosting bill. Pages are stored as files in the site's own GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket repository. Every save is a commit, and a free static host (GitHub Pages, GitLab Pages, Cloudflare Pages or Vercel) rebuilds the site. repositories.name: detectorscope
repositories.description: Build AI text detectors whose decisions are mechanistically grounded and human-auditable (EMNLP 2026)

paragraphs: DetectorScope turns a black-box AI text detector into one whose every prediction is a sum of named, validated features. It can tell you which properties of a text made it predict "AI" and where in the text they are located.
The pipeline: SAEs on the detector's residual stream, a description and validation score per feature, a threshold on that score, and a sparse head over the features that pass.

A DetectorScope detector is a concept bottleneck over interpretable sparse-autoencoder features: the language model's residual stream is encoded by SAEs, each feature gets a natural-language description that is validated against its own activations, and a sparse linear head over the validated features makes the decision. The prediction is therefore a sum of per-feature contributions, and every contribution has a description and a location in the text.
features: 🔍 Query a strong AI detector that is transparent about the features it uses
🖱️ Hover over the text to see the specific "AI Phrases" the detector is using
🔁 Convert your own black-box detector into an auditable one by using our pipeline
🎓 Analyze LLM Outputs so that you understand which models have which tendencies

repositories.name: zero-knowledge-demos
repositories.description: Interactive zero-knowledge proof playground: Schnorr, Fiat-Shamir, over-18 range proof, graph 3-colouring, Ali Baba cave, Waldo

paragraphs: An interactive playground for zero-knowledge proofs: prove you know a password, that you are over 18, that a graph can be 3-coloured, or where Waldo is, without revealing the secret. Every demo shows what goes over the wire and what the verifier learns. The cryptography is real (secp256k1 through @noble/curves, hashes through @noble/hashes) and runs entirely in your browser.
Try it: hermes98761234.github.io/zero-knowledge-demos
features: I know the password. Step through Schnorr identification (commit, challenge, response), run 20 rounds against a cheating prover who only passes by guessing the challenge, and watch the odds collapse. Then make it…

I am over 18. An issuer signs a Pedersen commitment to your age. You prove age - 18 lies in [0, 2^7) with a bit-decomposition range proof, each bit shown to be 0 or 1 by an OR-proof. Issuer, holder and verifier roles…

Graph 3-colouring. The Goldreich-Micali-Wigderson protocol as a game: hidden colours, the verifier picks an edge, two vertices are revealed, repeat. A non-3-colourable graph (K4) shows soundness growing round by round.
Ali Baba's cave and Where's Waldo. The two classic pictures, interactive, with a bluffing mode.
Light and dark themes, works at 375 px, inputs remembered in the browser, no server.

repositories.name: vanna
repositories.description: A model-driven options pricing, Greeks, and backtesting library — real Black-Scholes/binomial pricing and Greek-attributed P&L, not just historical-data buckets.

paragraphs: A model-driven options pricing, Greeks, and backtesting library — named after the real (if lesser-known) second-order Greek: the sensitivity of delta to volatility. Desktop GUI included.

No install, no server, no API key needed to try it — the live demo runs the real Python engine client-side via Pyodide (Python compiled to WASM), not a JS reimplementation. docs/vannasrc is kept in sync with vanna/pricing and vanna/backtest automatically (.github/workflows/sync-web-src.yml), so that claim can't quietly go stale.

I went looking at optopsy — a genuinely good, actively maintained, 1.5k-star options backtesting library — meaning to contribute a fix. What I actually came away with was a different itch: optopsy's statistics are empirical. It buckets real historical fills by DTE range and delta range and reports what happened in each bucket. That's a legitimate, useful approach, and it's also just not what I wanted, because it can tell you a trade made $340 without ever telling you why - how much of that was the stock moving, how much was time passing, how much was implied vol doing something ugly.

whatItDoes.text: A model-driven options pricing, Greeks, and backtesting library — named after the real (if lesser-known) second-order Greek: the sensitivity of delta to volatility. Desktop GUI included.

requirements.text: No install, no server, no API key needed to try it — the live demo runs the real Python engine client-side via Pyodide (Python compiled to WASM), not a JS reimplementation. docs/vannasrc is kept in sync with vanna/pricing and vanna/backtest automatically (.github/workflows/sync-web-src.yml), so that claim can't quietly go stale.
A transposed d1/d2 or a wrong sign in a formula copied from a textbook is an easy, quiet way to ship something subtly wrong; this way the tests catch it, not a user's P&L six months later.

No smile dynamics, no jumps, no real fill data. optopsy's data CLI (with a real EODHD subscription) is the right tool if you need that; a real historical-chain loader here is a legitimate v2, not a hidden gap.

repositories.name: symbolfit
repositories.description: Automatic parametric modeling with symbolic regression

paragraphs: Docs | Paper | Slides | Colab | pip | conda |
SymbolFit automatically finds closed-form functions that fit your data with uncertainty estimation, no manual guessing required.

SymbolFit was originally developed for experimental high-energy physics (HEP) analyses, but it works on any 1D, 2D, or higher-dimensional dataset where you need an interpretable parametric model with uncertainty estimates. You provide data points and SymbolFit returns a batch of candidate functions ranked by goodness-of-fit, each with optimized parameters and uncertainty estimates. All results are saved to CSV tables and PDF plots, ready for downstream use such as hypothesis testing in HEP.
features: Function search: PySR (symbolic regression) explores combinations of mathematical operators to discover functional forms that fit the data, without requiring a predefined template.
Re-optimization: LMFIT re-optimizes the numerical parameters in each candidate function and provides uncertainty estimates via covariance matrices.
Evaluation: every candidate is automatically scored (chi2/NDF, p-value, RMSE, R2), plotted with individual uncertainty variations and total uncertainty coverage, and saved to output files.

whatItDoes.text: Docs | Paper | Slides | Colab | pip | conda |

paragraphs: Type-safe search params state manager for Vue 3. A port of nuqs that uses Vue idioms: writable refs, v-model, reactive objects and a plugin.
⭐ Listed in Awesome Vue under State Management.

Filters, search terms, tabs, pagination and sort orders are state your users expect to share, bookmark and restore with the Back button. Storing that state in the URL makes it all work, but parsing and serializing query strings by hand is tedious and error-prone.
features: 🧩 The nuqs API: the same parsers, options and behaviour, adapted to Vue
🔒 Type-safe: typed state from parsers, with null removed by .withDefault()
✍️ Writable refs: assign .value or use v-model; .set() for options and promises
📦 Batched updates: changes in the same tick produce a single URL update
⏱️ Throttle & debounce: state is instant, URL writes are rate-limited

paragraphs: nginx-live-win32 is a portable ("green", unzip-and-run, no installation) Windows build of nginx + nginx-live-module. It provides a high-performance, low-latency open-source live streaming server supporting RTMP / Enhanced RTMP / HTTP-FLV publishing and playback.
The package also ships nginxservice.exe, which registers nginx as a Windows service and provides a system tray management UI.

The version number, build flags, executable size and SHA256 are generated automatically by the build scripts into BUILD-INFO.txt. That file is authoritative — do not edit it by hand, and do not hard-code versions here.

Enhanced RTMP v2 multi-track audio (Multitrack): several audio tracks forwarded in parallel
within one stream, each with its own cached sequence header replayed to joining players; the encapsulation is passed through as-is (no muxing, no transcoding)
HTTP-FLV publishing (POST) / playback (GET) with HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer

repositories.name: Insight
repositories.description: Oracle transparency and risk intelligence for DeFi: cross-source comparison, explainable assessments, and verifiable evidence for protocols and AI agents. Decision-input integrity for AI agents.

paragraphs: Insight is oracle transparency and risk infrastructure for DeFi and AI agents, built on BNB Smart Chain (BSC) and compatible with other EVM networks.

Insight helps DeFi applications, operators, developers, and AI agents inspect oracle prices and the risks of relying on them. It compares data from 10 oracle providers across 40+ blockchain networks, evaluates deviation, freshness, source independence, and protocol impact, and can issue signed evidence of its assessments. For AI agents specifically, this is decision-input integrity: a signed, re-verifiable answer to "can this price be trusted" before a trade is signed.

Insight is not a real-time oracle tracker. Price snapshots and feed health are collected every 15 minutes, reputation scores are recalculated hourly, and data is aggregated into daily reports. Check each assessment's freshness and validity window before using it.
features: Pre-Trade Safety Check — cross-oracle pre-trade verdict (PASS / CAUTION / DANGER / BLOCK) with signed EIP-712 attestation and a recommended maximum position size
Oracle Watch — continuous between-action monitoring with proceed / proceedwithcaution / halt recommendations
Agent-native payments — x402 pay-per-call in USDC on BNB Chain (AEON mandate flow) and a hosted MCP server at /api/mcp; registered ERC-8004 agent #375779
Verifiable evidence — independently verifiable signed receipts, plus opt-in ERC-8004 reputation anchoring of completed checks

whatItDoes.text: Insight is oracle transparency and risk infrastructure for DeFi and AI agents, built on BNB Smart Chain (BSC) and compatible with other EVM networks.

requirements.text: Metered calls use an X-API-Key; public receipt-verification endpoints do not require one.

The separately scoped scalar tensor companion in cryptanalysis adds binary/prime-field coordinate checks and Certicom ECCp-131 inputs. No Python execution path is introduced here and neither challenge is solved.

repositories.description: Run Gemma 4 E4B locally inside Obsidian via LiteRT-LM and WebGPU — private, offline, no API key, no Ollama, no server. paragraphs: Turn your notes into a living Karpathy LLM wiki. Chat with your vault, connect ideas, find gaps, and generate quizzes & flashcards — with Gemma 4 E4B running locally inside Obsidian. No API key, Ollama, or server.
⬇ Install from the community store ▶ See what it does · Step through the demo — nothing to install.

☔️ What do you do with everything you have already saved? Clipped articles. Saved posts. Course notes. Papers you meant to read. A vault that looks organised and is mostly unread — not because there is too much in it, but because there is no easy way to see what you've actually collected without opening things one at a time.
features: 🧠 Chat with one note or your whole vault — grounded in what you actually wrote, with sources listed by the plugin rather than generated by the model.
📇 A summary card for every note, and an index over all of them — so you can see what you have without opening anything.
🔗 Links between notes that turn out to be related — and tags drawn from one shared vocabulary rather than whatever each note happened to invent, which is what lets them find each other at all.
📚 Concept pages over the clusters that emerge — written above your notes, linking down into each one.
🔍 Gaps and contradictions surfaced — including claims in two notes that cannot both be true.

Reserved bottles — Mark bottles as "spoken for" (a birthday, a dinner) so suggestions and consume flows respect them
Drink-window alerts — Sommelier-curated maturity windows per wine and vintage; alerts when bottles approach peak, are in window, or slipping past it

repositories.name: neural-magic-eye
repositories.description: Neural Magic Eye: Learning to See and Understand the Scene Behind an Autostereogram, arXiv:2012.15692.

paragraphs: Official PyTorch implementation of the preprint paper "NeuralMagicEye: Learning to See and Understand the Scene Behind an Autostereogram", arXiv:2012.15692.

An autostereogram, a.k.a. magic eye image, is a single-image stereogram that can create visual illusions of 3D scenes from 2D textures. This paper studies an interesting question that whether a deep CNN can be trained to recover the depth behind an autostereogram and understand its content. The key to the autostereogram magic lies in the stereopsis - to solve such a problem, a model has to learn to discover and estimate disparity from the quasi-periodic textures. We show that deep CNNs embedded with disparity convolution, a novel convolutional layer proposed in this paper that simulates…

In this repository, we provide the complete training/inference implementation of our paper based on Pytorch and provide several demos that can be used for reproducing the results reported in our paper. With the code, you can also try on your own data by following the instructions below.

whatItDoes.text: Official PyTorch implementation of the preprint paper "NeuralMagicEye: Learning to See and Understand the Scene Behind an Autostereogram", arXiv:2012.15692.

Its nonlinear-programming core began as a faithful port of Ipopt — the same filter line-search algorithm, console output, and option semantics, so anyone used to reading ipopt logs can drop in pounce without relearning where the numbers live — and it has since grown into a family of solvers sharing one numerical backbone:
(the Ipopt port), plus an active-set SQP path, for general smooth problems min f(x) s.t. gL ≤ g(x) ≤ gU, xL ≤ x ≤ xU.

second-order (SOCP), positive-semidefinite (SDP), and the non-symmetric exponential and power cones — each solved to the global optimum, with infeasibility certificates, warm starts, and post-optimal sensitivity.

Conic & quadratic — dedicated interior-point solvers for LP, convex QP,
Global optimization — certified global optima for nonconvex

repositories.name: TrueBill
repositories.description: AI ELECTRICITY BILL AUDITOR

paragraphs: TrueBill is an AI electricity-bill auditor. A user sends a bill (photo or PDF) to a Telegram bot. TrueBill reads it, retrieves the applicable official tariff, recalculates the charges with a deterministic Python engine, and replies with an audit: which charges match, which don't, why, the official source and its effective date, and a draft clarification request.
AI reads. Rules verify. Evidence explains. The LLM never does the arithmetic. Extraction and explanation use AI; every charge is recalculated by plain Python against the official tariff.
MVP scope: one Delhi discom (BSES Rajdhani Power Limited, BRPL), one tariff category (Domestic).

whatItDoes.text: TrueBill is an AI electricity-bill auditor. A user sends a bill (photo or PDF) to a Telegram bot. Upgrading from 8.3.x? gpCAM 8.4 targets fvgp = 4.8 and renames a few constructor kwargs (gp2Scaledaskclient → daskclient, gp2Scalelinalgmode → linalgmode, gpranknupdate → ranknupdate), and replaces calcinv=True with linalgmode="CholInv". Full migration notes are in HISTORY.rst.

gpCAM (gpcam.lbl.gov) is an API and software designed to make advanced Gaussian Process function approximation and autonomous data acquisition/Bayesian Optimization for experiments and simulations more accurate, faster, simpler, and more widely available. The tool is based on a flexible and powerful Gaussian process regression at the core. The flexibility stems from the modular design of gpCAM which allows the user to implement and import their own Python functions to customize and control almost every aspect of the software. repositories.description: Optimal Control for Switched Systems

paragraphs: OCS2 (Optimal Control for Switched Systems) is a C++ toolbox for formulating and solving nonlinear optimal control problems, with an emphasis on real-time Model Predictive Control (MPC) for robotics.

OCS2 handles general path constraints through Augmented Lagrangian or relaxed barrier methods. To facilitate the application of OCS2 in robotic tasks, it provides additional tools to set up the system dynamics (such as kinematic or dynamic models) and cost/constraints (such as self-collision avoidance and end-effector tracking) from a URDF model. The library also provides an automatic differentiation tool to calculate derivatives of the system dynamics, constraints, and cost. To facilitate deployment on robotic platforms, OCS2 provides tools for ROS interfaces. The toolbox’s efficient and…
features: SLQ: continuous-time constrained DDP (SLQ/DDP family)
iLQR: discrete-time constrained DDP
SQP: multiple-shooting SQP (QP subproblems via HPIPM/BLASFEO)
SLP: sequential linear programming (PIPG)
IPM: multiple-shooting nonlinear interior-point method

repositories.name: connection-odds
repositories.description: How often a US domestic connection is missed, by hub, airline, hour, month and layover. Built from BTS on-time data, Sep 2023 to Aug 2026.

paragraphs: How often is a US domestic connection missed, and how long a layover does a 95% chance take? This project pairs arrivals with departures on the same airline at the 30 busiest US airports from the BTS on-time data, September 2023 to August 2026, scores each pair against what actually happened, and puts the result in a lookup tool that runs in the browser.

Result: 17% of 45-minute connections were missed, against 20.0% estimated from the inbound delay alone; on a March to August 2026 holdout the logistic model's calibration error was 0.86 points, against 2.05 for that inbound-only shortcut.

repositories.name: ragdocs
repositories.description: A RAG chatbot that answers questions about any PDF you upload, using only what’s in the document, and shows the page each answer came from. If the answer isn’t in the PDF, it says “I don’t know” instead of making something up.

paragraphs: A RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) chatbot that answers questions about any PDF you upload. It answers only from what's in the document, shows the page each answer came from, and says "I don't know" when the answer isn't there, instead of making something up.

You can use it through a Streamlit chat UI or a FastAPI API. The retrieval part is written by hand (no LangChain): the PDF is split into overlapping chunks, embedded locally with sentence-transformers, stored in Chroma, and the closest chunks are sent to Gemini to write the answer. The code is split into api, services and core, so each step lives in its own file.

Built for anyone who needs quick, grounded answers from a long document — a manual, a textbook, a report — without manually searching through it page by page. Upload once, ask as many questions as needed, get answers with sources you can verify.
features: Upload any PDF and ask natural-language questions about its content
Retrieval-augmented answers — the LLM only answers from chunks actually retrieved from the document, and says "I don't know" when the answer isn't present
Every answer includes page-level source citations with a distance score for each chunk (lower = closer match)
Per-document isolation — each upload gets its own vector collection, so multiple documents never bleed into each other's answers
Local embeddings (sentence-transformers) — no API cost or external call for the retrieval step

repositories.name: css-element-queries
repositories.description: CSS Element-Queries aka Container Queries. High-speed element dimension/media queries in valid css.

paragraphs: Element Queries is a polyfill adding support for element based media-queries to all new browsers (incl. IE7+). It allows not only to define media-queries based on window-size but also adds 'media-queries' functionality depending on element (any selector supported) size while not causing performance lags due to event based implementation.
It's a proof-of-concept event-based CSS element dimension query with valid CSS selector syntax.
features: no performance issues since it listens only on size changes of elements that have element query rules defined through css. Other element query polifills only listen on window.onresize which causes performance issues and…
no interval/timeout detection. Truly event-based through integrated ResizeSensor class.
automatically discovers new DOM elements. No need to call javascript manually.
no CSS modifications. Valid CSS Syntax
all CSS selectors available. Uses regular attribute selector. No need to write rules in HTML/JS.

repositories.name: lucca-traffic-twin
repositories.description: 3D, hour-by-hour SUMO microsimulation of traffic in Lucca (Italy): OSM network, calibrated demand, critical junctions, deck.gl viewer

paragraphs: A 3D, hour-by-hour microsimulation of road traffic in Lucca (Italy) and the surrounding plain, built with Eclipse SUMO on the real OpenStreetMap network. It simulates a typical school weekday and a Saturday, 24 hours each, and ranks the junctions where traffic loses the most time.

The goal is a calibrated baseline for testing how traffic in Lucca could be improved: junction redesigns, new links, signal timing, school-time staggering, parking policy. Every vehicle (about 340,000 trips on a weekday) is simulated individually.

This is a model, not a live traffic feed. The demand is synthetic and calibrated to the few public traffic counts available (see Calibration and Limits). Rely on the ranking of critical points more than on the absolute delays.

paragraphs: This project is a simple proxy server that allows you to access the TMDB (The Movie Database) API from regions where it might be blocked by network providers, such as Jio in India.

The TMDB Proxy is a serverless function deployed on Vercel that acts as a middleman between your application and the TMDB API. It fetches data from the TMDB API and caches the responses in Redis for faster subsequent requests. This proxy server can be used in any application that needs to access the TMDB API, such as movie or TV show applications.
features: Unblocks TMDB API: Allows access to the TMDB API from regions where it might be blocked by network providers.
Caching: Caches API responses in Redis for faster subsequent requests.
Serverless: Deployed as a serverless function on Vercel, eliminating the need for server management.
CORS Support: Adds CORS headers to allow cross-origin requests from your application.

repositories.name: purposemesh
repositories.description: Purpose-bound authorization reference: RBAC + ABAC + ReBAC, row/field controls, fidelity gates, lifecycle governance, and a tested 100K synthetic-data path.

paragraphs: Implemented today in the local React/Fastify/PDP/SQLite path; external enforcement requires a conformant adapter with published, target-version-scoped passing evidence, target apply, and verified read-back.

PurposeMesh is an open-source Technical Preview for authorization enforcement assurance across shared data. It combines a small RBAC capability vocabulary with ABAC scope and ReBAC relationships, then returns server-enforced row, field, purpose, classification, and lifecycle obligations.

Its core policy envelope is a Contract Capsule: one reviewable unit that keeps action, data scope, fields, purpose, conditions, approvals, and expiry together as policy moves across applications and platforms.

repositories.name: football-player-scouting
repositories.description: We're losing X. Who replaces him? Ranked, priced replacement shortlists for Big-5 clubs, built on twelve seasons of data and validated by replaying ten years of real transfers against the clubs' actual signings.

repositories.name: Megatron
repositories.description: Floor & Ceiling — NFL fantasy projections: PyTorch quantile transformer, walk-forward evals, self-updating GitHub Pages draft board

paragraphs: NFL fantasy football projections: a small quantile transformer (trained on a free Kaggle T4) versus classical baselines, evaluated honestly with walk-forward backtests, published as a static site that updates itself weekly during the season.

The site is four pages, no backend and no framework: a draft board with a pick-time optimizer that reads a live Sleeper draft, a trade calculator, weekly projections with p10/p50/p90 bands, and an about page carrying the backtest numbers. Models predict raw stat lines; fantasy points are computed from those by pure scoring functions, so PPR, half-PPR, standard and this league's custom rules all derive from one set of predictions.
Start here: docs/case-study.md, a two-page overview of what was built, how the numbers are kept honest and what they say. The full record is docs/methodology.md.

paragraphs: SideCar is a free, self-hosted VS Code extension that serves as a drop-in replacement for GitHub Copilot and Claude Code. Use local Ollama models, the Anthropic API, OpenAI, Fireworks AI, OpenRouter, Google Gemini, Groq, AWS Bedrock, your GitHub Copilot subscription, or any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, a gateway) for AI-powered coding — with full agentic capabilities, inline completions, and tool use.
A free, open-source, local-first autonomous AI agent for coding — a full agent loop, not just chat. No subscription, and with local models, no data leaves your machine.

Agent mode, tool use, and MCP are table stakes in 2026 — Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, Cline, and Continue all have them. What sets SideCar apart is the combination underneath, all with no subscription:
features: Genuinely free and fully local-first — runs offline on Ollama with no API key or required cloud; plug in a frontier provider only when you want one.

Tool-call recovery from model text — many capable local models emit their tool calls as plain text or JSON in the content field instead of the structured toolcalls field, so a stock harness sees no call and stalls.…

Capability-adaptive gates — completion, syntax, red-check, grounding, and citation gates plus tiered reprompt budgets aimed at making weaker local models usable. Whether the net effect is a lift is measured, not assumed.
Parallelism & write-isolation — shadow workspaces (ephemeral git worktree), audit mode (in-memory write buffer), fork & parallel solve (N attempts, pick the winner), and typed sub-agent facets.
First-party VS Code integration — Problems-panel security/diagnostics, Test Explorer agent runs, CodeLens actions, file decorations, inline completions, and inline chat.

repositories.name: rasbur
repositories.description: Auto-detecting multi-layer string decoder. Identifies the encoding, unwraps stacked layers, and says when it isn't sure.

paragraphs: Rasbur identifies what an encoded string is, decodes it, and keeps unwrapping stacked layers until nothing is left. You do not tell it the format.

Every decoder is scored twice: once on whether the input looks like its format, and again on whether the decoded output looks like real data. That second score is what separates a correct decode from one that merely looks valid, and it is why Rasbur returns nothing instead of guessing when it cannot tell.

whatItDoes.text: Rasbur identifies what an encoded string is, decodes it, and keeps unwrapping stacked layers until nothing is left. You do not tell it the format.

repositories.name: Benzi
repositories.description: Benzi is code intelligence infrastructure for AI models. It compiles your codebase into a resolved, queryable map of calls, data flow, control flow and class hierarchy first; then it reads, explains, runs, edits and verifies your code using it. Every language runs its own tree-sitter grammar into the same query map.

paragraphs: Language Agnostic · Model Agnostic · Compiles Locally · BYOK · MCP Compatible

Most AI coding agents grep and glob raw source code into AI model's context window and hope the model finds what matters. Benzi parses every file first — a real compiler, built on tree-sitter — into a precise, queryable map. Every symbol, every call edge, every reference, every class in its inheritance chain. One pass, done.

Every file parsed, imports resolved, class ancestry built, every identifier traced to its definition — before a single question is answered. Call flow and data flow join at every call site, so a bad value traces to its origin in one tool call. Claude Code greps; Cursor embeds; Aider maps signatures; Benzi resolves — in O(1). Ten languages so far, plus a markup engine for HTML, CSS, and DOM-JS — see Language support. Benzi is free to use during beta.
features: Six states, never a guess — every call site and every file carries one: resolved (proven in-repo edge), external (into a library, with the import evidence), candidate (ambiguous — the bounded set of possible targets,…
Runtime tracer — hooks every call during execution and overlays the observations back onto the static map.
Reasoning you can click — the same map that drives the tools drives a live call graph beside the chat; when the agent names a function, that node lights up.
Persistent memory — durable per-repo facts survive restarts; conventions learned once aren't re-derived every session.
Dual-engine: code + markup — a separate index for HTML/CSS/DOM-JS with cascade resolution and selector specificity, including frontend embedded inside Python strings.

whatItDoes.text: Language Agnostic · Model Agnostic · Compiles Locally · BYOK · MCP Compatible

repositories.name: inkstone
repositories.description: Local-first novel-to-comic generator — free, no GPU, pluggable providers.

paragraphs: Inkstone reads a local txt novel and, through the free Agnes multimodal API, produces comic pages with cross-panel character consistency — exported as PDF / CBZ / PNG. No GPU, no paid plan: just one free API key.

These panels were generated from the bundled sample (examples/scene1.txt) with the default L1+L2 pipeline — no L3, straight from the model. Consistency here is "medium" by design: the honest ceiling of a free, no-GPU model. More samples, including the full webtoon strip, are at:

Every novel-to-comic tool we surveyed in 2026 runs on a paid model — Gemini, OpenAI, Doubao, Wenxin, or Claude. Inkstone is built differently: it is Agnes-native and zero-cost, the one combination no other open-source generator occupies.
features: Free & local-first — one AGNESAPIKEY, no GPU, no paid plan.
Agnes-native multimodal — agnes-3.0-flash for scripting, agnes-image-2.5-flash for t2i and i2i consistency.
Pluggable ImageProvider — Agnes by default; PROVIDER=openaicompat for Agnes-protocol-compatible /images/generations gateways (i2i uses extrabody.image).
Character consistency engine — L1 prompt hard-description + L2 reference img2img, the robust path under no-GPU. An optional L3 PIL/OpenCV face overlay is off by default (opt-in via INKSTONEL3=1).
Reliability layer — token-bucket rate limiting, exponential-backoff retries, and error collection against 429/503.

whatItDoes.text: Inkstone reads a local txt novel and, through the free Agnes multimodal API, produces comic pages with cross-panel character consistency — exported as PDF / CBZ / PNG. No GPU, no paid plan: just one free API key.

requirements.text: The strongest approaches (IP-Adapter / InsightFace) need a local GPU running SDXL/Flux — incompatible with Inkstone's zero-cost premise.

repositories.name: printable_binary
repositories.description: A bijective mapping of all bytes to human-readable, terminal/editor-compatible UTF8 (ASCII-printable stays, delimiter chars -> similar-looking UTF8, control chars -> semantically-relevant UTF8 glyphs). C, Zig, Rust, LuaJIT, WASM & Node.js; working demo @ https://pmarreck.github.io/printable_binary/

paragraphs: A cross-platform utility with LuaJIT, C, Zig, Roc, JavaScript/Node, Rust, WebAssembly, and Cosmopolitan Actually Portable Executable (APE) variants for encoding arbitrary binary data into human-readable UTF-8 text, and then decoding it back to the original binary data.

PrintableBinary is designed to [de]serialize binary data to/from a visually distinct, human-readable format that is also copy-pastable and embeddable in any UTF-8-aware context. It's an alternative to hexadecimal encoding that offers better visual density and makes embedded ASCII text immediately recognizable, while also making it possible to incorporate binary data into text-based formats (such as JSON, TOML, XML, YAML, etc.) without escaping issues.
features: Multiple Implementations: Available as a LuaJIT script, native C CLI, Cosmopolitan APE, Zig CLI, Roc CLI, JavaScript module/Node CLI, WebAssembly CLI, and Rust raw codec for maximum flexibility
Web & Node.js Tooling: Drag-and-drop browser interface and a Node-based CLI wrapper share the same encode/decode core for cross-platform workflows
Visually Distinct Characters: Each of the 256 possible byte values maps to a unique, visually distinct UTF-8 character
ASCII Passthrough: Standard printable ASCII characters (32-126) largely remain themselves for immediate recognition
Shell-Safe Encoding: Special characters that could cause shell issues are encoded with safe Unicode alternatives

whatItDoes.text: A cross-platform utility with LuaJIT, C, Zig, Roc, JavaScript/Node, Rust, WebAssembly, and Cosmopolitan Actually Portable Executable (APE) variants for encoding arbitrary binary data into human-readable UTF-8 text, and then decoding it back to the original binary data.

paragraphs: A JavaScript engine written entirely in safe Rust, with zero unsafe, that reproduces the behavior of QuickJS 2026-06-04.

Within the Test262 scope that QuickJS 2026-06-04 runs, quickjs-oxide passes 83,304 of 83,562 variants (99.691%). QuickJS's test262.conf skips the other 18,475 of the 102,037 variants; across the full corpus the pass rate is 81.641%.

unsafecode = "forbid", so the compiler rejects unsafe anywhere in the engine, the CLI and the WebAssembly bindings. The garbage collector, compiler, VM, regular expression engine and Unicode tables are all safe Rust; the only third-party code in the engine is num-bigint and num-traits for BigInt arithmetic.

Cross-platform compatibility: All packages target net10.0 for modern .NET runtime support.
Multi-database support: Built-in dialects for SQL Server, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL, and Oracle; host applications register only what they use.
Modular components: Decoupled libraries for core utilities, data, caching, business logic, and API hosting.

repositories.name: mlkem-native
repositories.description: Secure, fast, and portable C90 implementation of ML-KEM / FIPS 203

paragraphs: mlkem-native is a secure, fast, and portable C90[^C90] implementation of ML-KEM[^FIPS203]. It is a fork of the ML-KEM reference implementation[^REF].

All C code in mlkem/src/ and mlkem/src/fips202/, except for the backends for platforms other than AArch64 and x8664 and the debug code, is proved memory-safe (no memory overflow) and type-safe (no integer overflow) using CBMC[^CBMC]. All AArch64 and x8664 assembly is proved to be functionally correct, memory-safe, and of secret-independent timing (constant-time), using HOL-Light[^HOL-Light].
mlkem-native includes native backends for Arm (64-bit, Neon), Intel/AMD (64-bit, AVX2), RISC-V (64-bit, RVV), and POWER (ppc64le, VSX). See benchmarks for performance data.

whatItDoes.text: mlkem-native is a secure, fast, and portable C90[^C90] implementation of ML-KEM[^FIPS203]. It is a fork of the ML-KEM reference implementation[^REF].

repositories.name: edgeparse
repositories.description: EdgeParse converts any digital PDF into Markdown, JSON (with bounding boxes), HTML, or plain text — deterministically, without a JVM, without a GPU, and with best-in-class accuracy on the 200-document benchmark suite included in this repository.

paragraphs: Fastest PDF extraction engine. Rust-native. No ML stack required for born-digital PDFs; optional in-browser OCR for image tables.
Extract Markdown, JSON (with bounding boxes), and HTML from any born-digital PDF — deterministically, in milliseconds, on CPU.
Never claim a win for engines not finished (Marker, MinerU, Nutrient, Unstructured partial). Benchmark details
features: How accurate is it? — Two labeled boards (2026-10-01, Apple M4 Max, 200 docs):
Official odl-bench (mean(NID,TEDS,MHS)): EdgeParse hybrid 0.900 (leads every finished metric), deterministic 0.857, WASM 0.854.
EdgeParse harness: deterministic 0.782 overall at 0.019 s/doc.
How fast? — 0.02 s/doc deterministic on Apple M4 Max for the 200-document corpus. Hybrid mode is slower (0.81 s/doc) when pages route to a local Docling Fast backend.

Does it need a GPU or Java? — No. No JVM, no GPU, no Python runtime for the CLI. Born-digital PDFs need no OCR models; optional PP-OCRv6 runs in-browser or on Node for image tables. Single 15 MB binary.

whatItDoes.text: Fastest PDF extraction engine. Rust-native. No ML stack required for born-digital PDFs; optional in-browser OCR for image tables.

repositories.name: Price-Pilot-Ai
repositories.description: This project is a high-performance AI-Powered Dynamic Pricing & Inventory Intelligence Platform. It is designed to help e-commerce businesses maximize their profit margins and optimize stock levels using real-time market data and machine learning.

paragraphs: An autonomous, multi-channel e-commerce pricing optimization and inventory intelligence platform powered by LangGraph multi-agent swarms, Bayesian price elasticity modeling, Prophet time-series forecasting, and conversational RAG copilots.

PricePilot AI is a production-grade, full-stack revenue optimization and inventory intelligence platform engineered for multi-channel e-commerce businesses. Modern merchants selling across independent direct-to-consumer (D2C) storefronts and high-velocity marketplaces (Amazon, Flipkart, Shopify, WooCommerce) face severe margin erosion from static markup heuristics, unpredictable competitor repricing, supply chain stockouts, and black-box pricing opacity.

PricePilot AI solves this through a decoupled three-tier microservice architecture that combines Bayesian price elasticity estimation, Facebook Prophet time-series forecasting, LangGraph multi-agent competitor swarms, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) copilots with Explainable AI (XAI) decision narratives.
features: Binary Search Gross Profit Maximizer: Mathematically locates the exact unit price point that maximizes total expected profit while respecting minimum margin floors and maximum markup ceilings.
Dynamic Price Elasticity Estimation: Estimates category-specific price sensitivity ($\epsilon$) using historical sales volume, competitor price differentials, and composite demand multipliers.
Interactive What-If Scenario Simulator (WhatIfSimulator.jsx):
Strategic Verdict Badges: Classifies proposed simulations into intuitive strategies (Margin Maximizer, Market Share Grab, Margin Risk, Volume Loss Risk).
Simple & Advanced Simulation Modes: High-level sliders for target price, competitor counter-moves, and demand multipliers alongside granular COGS overrides and time horizons.

whatItDoes.text: An autonomous, multi-channel e-commerce pricing optimization and inventory intelligence platform powered by LangGraph multi-agent swarms, Bayesian price elasticity modeling, Prophet time-series forecasting, and conversational RAG copilots.

paragraphs: Erstes Stück (Wurzel) der Kürzeste-Wege-Linie der "Konzepte"-Reihe für die Website "Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning": anders als die Fall-Demos im Portfolio (ein Anwendungsfall, mehrere Verfahren im Vergleich) zeigt diese Demo ein Verfahren – die Breitensuche (BFS) – an einem wachsenden Beispiel. Vom Start aus werden erst alle Nachbarn besucht, dann deren Nachbarn – Schicht für Schicht; das Ziel ist gefunden, sobald es zum ersten Mal entdeckt wird, und seine Route hat garantiert die wenigsten Kanten. Der Haken steckt im Wort: BFS zählt Kanten, nicht Kosten.

Einordnung in die Reihe (die Kanten des Graphen): die Wurzel ist bewusst die einfachste Suche im Netz. Ihre Schwäche – Kosten werden ignoriert – ist der Ansatzpunkt des nächsten Stücks (Dijkstra: Kosten korrekt, aber blind in alle Richtungen); die Suche in alle Richtungen und die Anfrage von vorn sind die Ansatzpunkte von Bidirektionaler Suche und Contraction Hierarchies. Inzwischen sind auch die Nachfolger gebaut (siehe Baum).

In den bisherigen Stücken gab es zwei Seiten (Fahrzeuge und Aufträge) – man nennt das bipartit. Hier gibt es eine Gruppe von Fahrern: je zwei können zusammen fahren (Fahrgemeinschaften), wenn ihre Fahrzeit…

Wichtigster Befund der Vorarbeit: die Geschichte „ohne Blüten verliert die Suche viele Paare“ ist auf realistischen Karten schwächer, als sie klingt. Die faire Baseline ist Edmonds' Waldsuche ohne den Kontraktionsschritt (die wörtliche Breitensuche der Zweiseiten-Demo liefert auf einem allgemeinen Graphen nicht einmal gültige Wege, das wäre ein Strohmann): sie verliert Paare nur auf einem Teil der Karten, meist eines, und der Verlust hängt an der Nummerierung der Fahrer. Der stärkere Befund ist der Beweis: ohne Kontraktion lässt sich selbst ein richtiges Ergebnis fast nie beweisen. Deshalb…

Einordnung in die Reihe (die Kanten des Graphen): dieses Stück lockert die Annahme „zwei getrennte Seiten“ der Verbesserungswege. Seine eigenen Schwächen sind die Ansatzpunkte des nächsten Stücks: keine Gewichte (Gewichteter Blossom: Ungarisch + Blossom).

repositories.name: shadow-map
repositories.description: 🌗💡Shadow Map is an interactive technical demo that visualises how directional light shadows work in real-time 3D rendering. It combines a custom Three.js scene with a scroll-driven narrative powered by GSAP

paragraphs: A scroll-driven 3D experience that renders real-time shadow mapping with Three.js.

Shadow Map is an interactive technical demo that visualises how directional light shadows work in real-time 3D rendering. It combines a custom Three.js scene with a scroll-driven narrative powered by GSAP, guiding the viewer through the core concepts of shadow mapping — from the directional light source to the PCF filtering that produces soft edges.

The experience begins with a wide, atmospheric landscape. As the user scrolls, the camera lifts to reveal a monumental "THREE.JS" inscription, then transitions into an overlay that explains each component of the shadow pipeline through horizontally scrolling cards.
features: Real-time shadows — Directional light casting shadows at 4096×4096 resolution with PCF (Percentage-Closer Filtering) for soft edges.
Scroll-driven narrative — A cinematic camera move followed by a fade transition into an educational overlay, all synchronised with the user's scroll via GSAP ScrollTrigger.
Animated wildlife — Six horses, a flamingo, a stork, and a parrot roam the scene, each with looped morph animations that play asynchronously.
3D typography — A bold, beveled "THREE.JS" text geometry sits embedded in the terrain, acting as the visual anchor of the scene.
Shadow map HUD — Press T to toggle an inset view of the shadow map texture, revealing exactly what the light sees.

whatItDoes.text: A scroll-driven 3D experience that renders real-time shadow mapping with Three.js.

paragraphs: A web-based tool to generate V2Ray configurations for multiple IP addresses or ranges, supporting VMESS, VLESS, WireGuard, and Trojan protocols.

The V2Ray Config Modifier is an HTML and JavaScript-based application designed to help users generate multiple V2Ray configurations efficiently. Users can input existing VMESS, VLESS, WireGuard, or Trojan configurations, specify IP addresses or ranges, or choose from predefined IP ranges of popular CDN providers like Cloudflare, Gcore, and Fastly. The tool generates new configurations for each IP address or range.
features: VMESS, VLESS, WireGuard, and Trojan Support: Accepts VMESS, VLESS, WireGuard, and Trojan configurations as input.
WireGuard Config Conversion: Converts standard WireGuard [Interface] / [Peer] configs to wireguard:// URLs, including multiple configs at once.

repositories.description: a2ui-vue | Vue 3 implementation of A2UI protocol. Enabling AI agents to render dynamic, interactive user interfaces in Vue applications.

paragraphs: a2ui-vue is a community Vue 3 renderer for the A2UI (Agent-to-UI) open protocol, fully supporting the official A2UI v0.9 specification. It enables AI agents to express UI intent as structured JSON and have it rendered as rich, interactive components inside any Vue 3 application — with no HTML/CSS knowledge required by the agent.

A2UI (Agent-to-UI) is an open protocol that defines how AI agents communicate UI intent to a frontend renderer. Instead of generating raw HTML/CSS, an agent emits typed JSON messages ("show a card with title X and a list of Y"). The renderer translates those messages into real visual components.
a2ui-vue is the community Vue 3 implementation of this protocol:
features: Decouples agent logic from frontend implementation details
Lets AI agents describe interface intent with structured JSON instead of raw HTML
Gives Vue teams a native renderer with TypeScript, theming, and component reuse
Makes agent-generated UI more deterministic, inspectable, and maintainable
20+ built-in components (layout, content, media, inputs)

repositories.name: Competitor-Insight-Engine
repositories.description: AI-powered tool that scrapes any company's website, finds real-time competitors via Tavily search, and generates a full competitive intelligence report — including market comparison and strategic recommendations — using any LLM of your choice.

paragraphs: Give it one company URL; get back a full competitor analysis report in 90 seconds.

▶ Live demo: competitor-insight-engine.vercel.app — opens on recorded real runs, so no keys are needed to watch it work. Bring your own model key (Groq/Gemini have free tiers) to run it against a company of your choice; it never leaves your browser.

Competitive research is usually manual: open a dozen browser tabs, read each company's site, take notes, and hand-build a comparison table. It's slow and it goes stale the moment a new competitor appears.
features: One-input analysis — a single company URL produces a complete Markdown report.
Live competitor discovery — Tavily web search finds current competitors, not a hardcoded list.
Two-layer competitor filtering — an LLM ranks candidates, then a hard-coded domain blocklist rejects forums/news/review sites, so only real companies survive.
Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) — pick a provider + model in the UI and paste your key; it's held in sessionStorage and sent browser → backend only. Never stored, logged, or seen by the hosting layer.
Six LLM providers, one code path — Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral, and local Ollama, all through a single OpenAI-compatible client. Switching models changes no code.

whatItDoes.text: Give it one company URL; get back a full competitor analysis report in 90 seconds.

repositories.name: brookmd
repositories.description: Zero-dep streaming markdown for the browser — Rust→WASM, 100% CommonMark 0.31 + GFM. Built to not melt the main thread on concurrent LLM streams.

paragraphs: Streaming markdown for every platform. One Rust core — incremental parse with speculative closure for mid-stream constructs, stable block identities so unchanged blocks never re-reconcile — compiled to WASM for the web and to native libraries for mobile and desktop. Every boundary emits the same versioned JSON wire, byte-for-byte. 100% CommonMark 0.31 + GFM — 652/652 and 24/24 byte-exact against the reference renderers.
In the browser, wire each LLM stream to a BrookClient and the markdown renders incrementally off the main thread, block by block — so many concurrent streams render without melting the UI thread.
features: Off the main thread — a pooled Web Worker per stream; the parser re-parses

only the active tail on each token, patches cross the worker boundary as verified splices (emitted bytes stay O(n) even for one giant growing block — wire delta mode, contract v1.2.0), and heavy renderers (highlighting,…
SSR-safe — imports and renderToString cleanly on the server across React,
Vue, Solid, and Svelte; the worker is created lazily on the client.
Structured block.data channel (opt-in, default off) — tables, headings,

One Rust core — incremental parse with speculative closure for mid-stream constructs, stable block identities so unchanged blocks never re-reconcile — compiled to WASM for the web and to native libraries for mobile and desktop. repositories.name: NLLB_translator
repositories.description: Multi-engine neural translator across 200 languages — local NLLB-200 / MADLAD / Ollama + free Gemini/Groq APIs. FastAPI + Next.js.

paragraphs: A multi-engine translator across 200 languages — open models on your own server, or cloud models with your own key, all from one clean UI.

Pick the translation engine per request: NLLB-200, Tencent's Hy-MT2, TranslateGemma 4B, Qwen3.5 2B, and Qwen3 1.7B run inside the Space (no third-party API or key needed). TranslateGemma and the two small Qwen models use a bundled Ollama server. Cloud models — Gemini, Qwen and GPT-OSS on Groq, anything on OpenRouter, or OpenAI's low-cost GPT-6 Luna — work with your own key. A FastAPI backend with a small provider registry does the routing; a Next.js + Tailwind frontend puts it all on one surface.
This is a v2 rebuild of the original Gradio-based NLLB translator, re-architected into a multi-engine FastAPI + Next.js web app.
features: Multiple engines, one UI — switch engines mid-session; local and cloud side by side, grouped.
200 languages — the full FLORES-200 set, with a searchable picker and common languages pinned.
No third-party API for local engines — all five local engines translate on the server; cloud engines are labelled with where the text goes.
Built for typing — debounced auto-translate, auto-growing panes, one-click example phrases, skeleton loading, swap, copy, dark mode.

Progressive output — LLM translations appear as tokens arrive; NLLB shows each completed line. Changing text or settings cancels the previous stream and keeps old responses from replacing the current result.

paragraphs: This project uses WebRTC DataChannels for peer-to-peer file transfer. GitHub stores the source code, Vercel serves the static frontend, and a small Node.js service on Render handles WebSocket signalling and the /ice-config endpoint.
features: Files are intended to travel over an encrypted WebRTC DataChannel between browsers when a direct connection succeeds.

repositories.name: twinwire
repositories.description: Multiplayer networking for browser games: one resumable session on two wires (WebSocket + WebRTC datagrams), a lobby, and netcode helpers. Works in every browser, iPhone Safari included.

paragraphs: Multiplayer networking for browser games. One player session, two wires: a WebSocket for what must arrive, and WebRTC datagrams (UDP-like: unordered, no retransmits) for what must arrive fast. Twinwire picks the fast wire when the network allows it, falls back to the WebSocket the moment it doesn't, and keeps the player's session (and seat) through dropped connections, app switches and Wi-Fi-to-cellular hand-offs. It comes with a lobby (room codes, quick play, ready-up) and the netcode helpers an authoritative-server game needs.

Browser games that want to feel good online hit the same wall: WebSocket is TCP, so one lost packet holds up every packet behind it, and on a phone that's a stutter. WebRTC data channels can be unreliable and unordered like UDP, but they're fiddly to set up, they fail on some networks, and a channel that says "open" isn't proof that packets get through. Then there's everything around it: reconnecting without losing your place, rooms and invite codes, interpolating other players, predicting your own.
Twinwire does that part, so the game can be the game:
features: Two wires, one session. WebSocket for the session; a WebRTC data channel for state, used only while probes prove
Sessions that survive. A dropped connection resumes the same session: same identity, same lobby seat, events
Events at UDP speed. Ordered, acknowledged JSON events go on the WebSocket and are mirrored on the datagram
State, latest wins. Binary state streams that coalesce and expire instead of queueing, up to 64 KiB, with
A lobby. Private rooms with codes, public quick play matched by mode and build, stable seats, host hand-off,

repositories.name: rulecast
repositories.description: Deliver project conventions to coding agents at the moment they matter.

paragraphs: Your project's conventions are written down in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, and your coding agent read them once, forty tool calls ago. rulecast delivers them again at the moment they matter: when the agent is about to break one.

A rule pairs a check with a message and a pointer to the doc section it enforces. rulecast runs as an agent hook, so when the agent changes a file that breaks a rule — with its edit tools or with Bash — it gets told, in the same turn, before it moves on.

A file the agent rewrites with sed -i or a script is checked like one it changes with Edit: rulecast compares the working tree before and after each Bash call. A change no call explains — your own editor, a formatter, a job the agent left running — is reported when the agent stops, and never blocks it.

whatItDoes.text: Your project's conventions are written down in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, and your coding agent read them once, forty tool calls ago. rulecast delivers them again at the moment they matter: when the agent is about to break one.

repositories.name: isms
repositories.description: The open-source management system built to stay alive, not rot after the audit. AI-first; documents in git, collaboration in PostgreSQL, ships as a single binary.

paragraphs: Because the ones we have are complex, opaque, and treated as a compliance exercise — relevant for the audit, irrelevant the day after. Meanwhile the stakes keep rising: in a world of accelerating AI adoption and expanding threat surfaces, a management system that doesn't stay alive is worse than useless.

We believe it doesn't have to work that way. Security done right starts at the root — genuinely understanding and managing your risks, not papering over them. Built from the ground up with an AI-first workflow and real discipline in design and use, a management system should be a living part of how you operate, not a burden on top of it.

That's why it's open source: built to work for organizations of all sizes — and finally a credible option for smaller ones, who've never had a management system that's simple, stays current, and doesn't fight them. We built this to change that.
features: Template scaffolding — Pick a standard, scaffold the documents, start writing. Templates provide structure; you own the content.
Multi-standard — Run ISO 27001 + ISO 14001 + HIPAA simultaneously in one organization.
Git-based documents — Markdown with YAML frontmatter. Full version history with diffs and blame.
Mermaid diagrams — Fenced mermaid blocks render as responsive diagrams while their Markdown source remains editable and version-controlled.
Review workflow — Round-based review, inline suggestions, approval policies, auto-merge. See above.

repositories.name: withme-starter
repositories.description: Find your people in what you love to do. An open-source starter for apps where people meet in person.

paragraphs: An open-source starter for apps where people meet in person around something they love: tap someone's tag or scan their code, nothing to install, and you stay connected long after the moment that brought you together. It ships as a web app and an iOS and Android app over one API, ready to remix.
It grew out of Vibe With Me, for the people you meet at shows. Golf is my other passion, so the first remix is Golf With Me. This repo is a way to remix the idea for whatever you love.

Why. In Bowling Alone, Robert Putnam traced how the leagues and clubs that built America's social capital thinned out: generational change did the most, television about a quarter, sprawl and busier lives about a tenth each. Join or Die, the documentary about his work, carries that into a world of feeds built to hold attention, not bring people together. Putnam's remedy is plain: join something. Shared pastimes build the kind he calls bridging social capital, where people who differ on everything else meet over the one thing they share. This starter is a small push in that direction: every…

repositories.name: granite-flyway
repositories.description: Moved: Granite Flyway is now Flightline → vikqazi.github.io/flightline

paragraphs: A waterfowl map for New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Maine and Rhode Island, 2026–27 season. Formerly Granite Flyway.
Turn on one state or several. Neighbouring states meet on the same Census border line, so there are no gaps or overlaps at a state line.

Zone polygons are not sketched. They are routed along the actual roads named in each state's written boundary description (Maine's Coastal Zone is the state's own polygon), and each state's zones add up to its outline exactly. Maine's 2026–27 North/South line is the newly adopted Route 2 line; the state's printed zone map and GIS layer still show the old one, which the app draws dotted for comparison. Rhode Island sets every season statewide except the late Canada goose season, so its two areas follow the late-season goose line: the named roads on land, and RIDEM's own line across the bay.

repositories.name: UMM-Reflection
repositories.description: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models: reflection SFT and multi-round Flow-GRPO RL for BAGEL

paragraphs: UMM-Reflection teaches a unified understanding-and-generation model (BAGEL-7B-MoT) to look at its own image, decide whether it is done, and, if not, write an edit and render a corrected image, all inside one model and one context. Reinforcement learning runs on complete reflection trajectories: sibling trajectories share one first image, so the group-relative advantage compares reflection strategies, and one trajectory-level advantage updates both the reflection tokens and the flow-based revisions. No critic or verifier is used at inference.

repositories.name: bunster
repositories.description: Compile shell scripts to static binaries.

paragraphs: A shell compiler that converts shell scripts into secure, portable, and static binaries. Unlike other tools (i.e. shc), Bunster does not just wrap your script within a binary. It literally compiles them to standalone shell-independent programs.
Under the hood, Bunster transpiles shell scripts into Go code. Then it uses the Go Toolchain to compile the code to an executable.
Bunster aims to be compatible with bash as a starting move. Expect that most bash scripts will just work with bunster. Additional shells will be supported as soon as we release v1.
features: Static binaries: scripts compiled with bunster are not just wrappers around your script, nor do they rely on any external shells on your system.
Modular: unlike traditional shells scripts that are written in a single file, bunster offers a module system that allows you to distribute code across as many files as needed. learn more
Package Manager: bunster has a builtin package manager that makes it easy to publish and consume modules as libraries. learn more
Native .env files support: .env files are natively supported in bunster, allowing you to load variables from .env files at runtime. learn more

Static assets embedding: bunster allows you to embed files and directories within your compiled program at compile time. Simply use them as if they were normal files in the system at runtime. learn more

repositories.description: A responsive browser-based paired samples t test calculator with p-values, confidence intervals, effect size, paired visualization, and APA-style results.

paragraphs: Paired T-Test Calculator is a lightweight, browser-based statistics tool for comparing two related sets of measurements. It is designed for students, researchers, analysts, educators, and anyone who needs to run a paired-samples t test without installing statistical software or sending data to a remote calculation service. A typical use case is a before-and-after study in which the same participants are measured twice, but the same workflow also applies to matched pairs and repeated measurements under two related conditions.

The project focuses on completing the practical task around the statistical test, not merely producing a p-value. Users can see the exact row-by-row pairing, review the calculated differences, obtain descriptive and inferential statistics, visualize paired changes, copy an APA-style result, and download the calculated values as CSV. The interface is responsive and works on desktop and mobile screens. It is implemented entirely with static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript so it can be hosted directly with GitHub Pages.

🧠 Adaptive Optimizations: Uses shader translation, render state caching, uniform batching, and bundle reuse for efficiency.

paragraphs: A clean, responsive web application for tracking weekly and monthly income and expenses. WeeklyBudget combines a polished sage-green interface with period-based analytics, an interactive calendar, multilingual support, optional Firebase cloud sync, and downloadable budget reports.

📊 Period-Aware Analytics — Category breakdowns, spending charts, top categories, largest expenses, averages, and transaction counts update automatically for the selected week or month.
📅 Interactive Calendar View — Browse daily income and expense totals in a monthly calendar, select any date to review its transactions, and quickly add entries for that day.

Document Loader: Supports local file loading, with web crawling capabilities under development.

repositories.name: matrix-engine-wgpu
repositories.description: WebGpu powered PWA App.Crazy fast rendering solution.Visual Scripting.Yatzy with real physics, MOBA 3d Forest of hollow blood

paragraphs: Author: Nikola Lukić 📧 zlatnaspirala@gmail.com 📅 Version: 2.0.0 Beta 2026 Alias The Beast

A WebGPU engine focused on performance that also mimics features from major engines, inspired by the original matrix-engine for WebGL. It uses the wgpu-matrix npm package as a replacement for gl-matrix to handle model-view-projection matrices.

Published on npm as matrix-engine-wgpu (the npm package is not always up to date, so cloning the GitHub repository is recommended). Since version [1.18.7], the npm package has been much more stable and usable. All examples can be run using the npm package, not just a GitHub clone. You can also use public providers like unpkg.com, etc. You can use PREFIX for textures or objects paths. The Beast works with CodePen. The worker physics bridge checks whether the host origin is external and adjusts resource paths accordingly; otherwise, it uses local resources. See codepen examples.
features: Backend editorX (App level+Shader VisualScripting) (works in local env - desktop browsers) support list: Chrome, Edge, Opera, Firefox desktop.
Code Creator (The Beast code generator) is standalone. It can be used publicly, but users must trust the page before entering an API key.
Canvas is dynamically created in JavaScript—no element needed in HTML.
Access the main scene objects:
Add meshes with .addMeshObj(), which supports OBJ loading, unlit textures, cubes, spheres, etc.
